en: Three More Snapshots
zh: 再补三幅剪影

children: Three more snapshots bring the contours of Byzantine Romanness into focus and fill in more of the picture outlined by the five snapshots offered at the head of Chapter 1. What personal and social “content” made someone a Roman in Byzantium, beyond the formal labels of state (being a subject of the “emperor of the Romans”) and law (being a Roman citizen)?

. The historian Agathias, writing around 580, presented an idealized image of contemporary Frankish society. He did this by, first, postulating that they were in all ways similar to “us” (i.e., “the Romans”), and then noting some of the ways in which they differed. This parity did not, however, remove the Franks from the category of “barbarians” in his eyes, but at least they were not nomads. I quote the passage and then extract its implications for the kind of group that the Romans constituted for Agathias.
再看三幅剪影，拜占庭罗马性的轮廓会更清楚，也能补充第1章开头五幅剪影初步勾勒的图景。除了国家和法律给出的正式身份，即身为“罗马人的皇帝”的臣民与身为罗马公民，个人及社会生活中还有哪些“内容”让一个人成为拜占庭的罗马人？
把法兰克人与罗马人并提。
约580年，史家阿加提阿斯描绘了一幅理想化的当代法兰克社会图景。他先假定他们在各方面都和“我们”（也就是罗马人）相似，再指出双方有些地方不同。在他看来，双方虽然相当，法兰克人却依然属于“蛮族”，不过至少不是游牧者。下面先引这段话，再据此分析阿加提阿斯把罗马人看成何种群体。

en: The Franks are not nomads, as some barbarians are, but their polity and laws are modeled on the Roman pattern, apart from which they uphold similar standards with regard to contracts, marriage, and religious observance. They are in fact all Christians and adhere to the strictest orthodoxy. They also have magistrates in their cities, priests, and celebrate the feasts in the same way as we do; and, for a barbarian people, they strike me as extremely well-bred, civilized, and as practically the same as ourselves except for their uncouth style of dress and peculiar language.
zh: 法兰克人不像某些蛮族那样是游牧者，他们的政治共同体与法律以罗马模式为范本，除此之外，他们在契约、婚姻和宗教礼仪方面也秉持类似的标准。他们事实上全是基督徒，恪守最严格的正教。他们的城市里也有行政官、司祭，并以与我们相同的方式庆祝节日；就一个蛮族民族而言，他们给我的印象是教养极好，也很文明。除了衣着粗陋、语言奇特，他们简直就和我们一样。

en: Agathias offers a global, comprehensive definition of who the Franks are as a people by deploying the categories of classical ethnography and applying them to a base-Roman template, which is then adjusted to reflect the distinctive aspects of Frankish culture and society. According to him, a people—today we might say an ethnic group or nation—is defined by its polity, laws, religion, customs, morality, language, and dress. The Franks and Romans are equivalent entities on this level: they fill out all the same questions on the census, but check different boxes under some of them. It is interesting that dress and language, rather than more abstract qualities such as politics and civilization, are singled out as the chief markers of difference between the two. Conversely, while religion is listed among the categories, Christianity is not a quality that can distinguish the Romans here, for the Franks shared that with them; it is instead dress and speech that chiefly mark difference.
zh: 阿加提阿斯先用古典民族志的范畴建立一个以罗马人为参照的框架，再据法兰克文化及社会的特点调整它，从而全面说明法兰克人是怎样一个群体。按照他的说法，一个人民共同体，也就是我们今天可能说的一个族群或民族，是由其政体、法律、宗教、习俗、道德、语言和服饰界定的。法兰克人与罗马人在这个层面上是对等的实体：他们在人口普查表上填写所有同样的问题，只是在某些问题下勾选不同的选项。有意思的是，被挑出来作为两者之间主要差异标记的，是服饰和语言，而不是政治与文明之类更抽象的品质。反过来，虽然宗教列在范畴之中，基督教却在这里不是能区分罗马人的品质，因为法兰克人与他们共享它；真正主要标记差异的是服饰与言语。

children: Yet kinship was also an issue. In Snapshot 3 of Chapter 1, Konstantinos VII saw the nations of the world as basically separate species of animals that should not intermarry, making one exception for unions between Romans and Franks. Even so, the two people did not have a common ancestry; they were a different
The twelfthcentury historian Ioannes Zonaras says something interesting about this. He quotes the sixth-century historian Prokopios of Kaisareia as saying that the Franks were not part of the Roman
because they belonged to the German

Prokopios had indeed said that the Franks were Germans, but he had not gone out of his way, as Zonaras does, to deny that they were related to the Romans; that would have been too obvious in the sixth century. In other words, Zonaras wanted to make it extra clear that Franks and Romans were not ethnically related, possibly in reaction to affirmations, such as we find in Agathias, of the “cultural kinship” between the two leading powers of the Christian world.
A Byzantine colony in ninth-century Italy.

An early twelfth-century addition to the history of Ioannes Skylitzes notes that Basileios I (867–886) founded the city of Kallipolis (Gallipoli) on the coast of southern Italy by resettling people there from the city of Herakleia on the Black Sea coast. “This explains why that city still uses Roman customs and dress and a thoroughly Roman social order, down to this day.”

“Roman” is again defined through the same ethnographic terms: one can tell who is a Roman and who is not by the presence or absence of mundane ethnic traits such as dress. Not everyone in Byzantine southern Italy was a Roman, and these, then, were the criteria by which one could tell the difference. The passage has two additional corollaries. First, it implies that a provincial population from the Black Sea coast, and not only the populace of Constantinople, could serve as a benchmark for Byzantine Romanness, especially when transplanted to Italy, where the population was ethnically diverse. Second, the author expects that, barring major disruption, the town’s ethnic profile would abide during the three centuries between its foundation and his own time. In the local Italian context, this implies a continuity in settlement. “The persistence of ‘local’ or ‘indigenous’ traits, habits, styles, and so on constitutes a kind of descent,”
and therefore a kind of ethnicity. The bishops of Gallipoli remained “Greek” until the later fourteenth century.
8. Saint Neilos is taken for a barbarian.

The tenth-century saint Neilos the Younger was from Rossano, Calabria, a predominantly Greekspeaking city in the farthest corner of the empire. One day he found a fox pelt thrown by the side of the road and, for reasons known only to himself, tied it around his head. In this way, he went around the town and no one recognized him. “Some children saw him dressed like that and began to throw stones at him, saying, ‘Hey you Bulgarian monk!,’ whereas others called him a Frank and some an Armenian.”

His vita does not explicitly say that he or his compatriots were Romans, but that was the implied standard against which ethnic difference was judged. As Florin Curta has observed about provincial Greek hagiographies, their “audience was ‘Roman.’ Clearly, there was no reason to stress the obvious.”
The common ethnonym was so immanent that it could be taken for granted, which must be factored into any analysis of its valence for the Byzantines.
然而亲属关系也是一个问题。在第一章剪影3中，君士坦丁七世把世界各民族看作基本上不应通婚的不同动物物种，只为罗马人与法兰克人的结合破了一次例。即便如此，这两个民族并没有共同祖先；他们属于不同的
（genos）。十二世纪史学家约翰·佐纳拉斯对此说了些有意思的话。他引用六世纪史学家凯撒利亚的普罗科匹厄斯的话说，法兰克人不属于罗马人的
（ethnos）。普罗科匹厄斯确实曾说法兰克人是日耳曼人，但他没有像佐纳拉斯那样特意否认他们与罗马人有亲属关系；那在六世纪太显而易见了。换言之，佐纳拉斯想格外明确地表示法兰克人与罗马人没有族群亲属关系，可能是对某种肯定说法的反应，比如我们在阿加提阿斯那里看到的、对基督教世界两大强权之间“文化亲属关系”的肯定。
九世纪意大利的一处拜占庭殖民点。
十二世纪初对约翰·斯基利齐斯史著的一段增补记载，瓦西里一世（867–886年在位）把黑海沿岸赫拉克利亚城的人口迁置到意大利南部海岸，建立了卡利波利斯（加利波利）城。“这解释了为什么那座城市至今仍然遵循罗马习俗，穿罗马服装，社会秩序也是彻底罗马式的。”

“罗马”再次通过同样的民族志术语来定义：凭服饰之类日常族群特征的有无，就能分辨谁是罗马人、谁不是。拜占庭的意大利南部并非人人都是罗马人，而这些就是分辨差异的标准。这段话还有两个推论。第一，它暗示黑海沿岸的行省人口——而不只是君士坦丁堡的民众——可以充当拜占庭罗马性的基准，尤其是在他们迁居族群多样的意大利之后。第二，作者预期，若无重大扰动，该镇的族群面貌会在建城到他本人时代之间的三个世纪里保持不变。在意大利地方语境中，这暗示了定居的连续性。“‘地方’或‘本土’特征、习惯、风格等等的持续存在构成了一种世系”，
因而也是一种族群性。加利波利的主教们直到十四世纪后期仍是“希腊人”。
十世纪圣徒小圣尼洛斯来自卡拉布里亚的罗萨诺，那是帝国最远角落一座以希腊语为主的城市。一天他在路边发现一张被丢弃的狐狸皮，出于只有他自己知道的原因，把它绑在头上。就这样他在城里走动，没人认出他。“一些孩子看见他这身打扮，开始朝他扔石头，喊‘喂，你这个保加利亚修士！’，另一些叫他法兰克人，还有一些叫他亚美尼亚人。”
他的圣徒传没有明说他或他的同胞是罗马人，但那是判断族群差异的隐含标准。正如弗洛林·库尔塔论行省希腊语圣徒传时所观察到的，它们的“受众是‘罗马人’。显然，没有理由强调显而易见之事”。
这个共同族名深入当地人的日常生活，以至于人人可以把它视为不言而喻。分析它对拜占庭人有何意涵时，必须把这一点考虑在内。

en: Whether we read an implied default Romanness into this passage or not, what is significant is that provincial populations, including children, were willing to make ethnic assignments based on headgear or other distinguishing peculiarities of appearance. It is a bad sign for the position of ethnic minorities in the empire that their first instinct was to throw stones at foreigners. But the point here concerns ethnic sensitivities and the way that provincials read ethnicity into apparel. Byzantine authors, for example the emperor Konstantinos VII (Snapshot 3), typically refer to the “customs” of the Romans that, among other traits, defined them as a nation. Language was one such trait and dress was another. A son of the Bulgarian tsar Petar, returning from a stay at the Roman court, was killed by a Bulgarian border guard because he was wearing Roman clothing.

This may have been a reference to elite court dress. But there are stories that take us down the social ladder. We hear of spies sent out by the Persians and later the Muslims who were “dressed like Romans,” could speak the Roman language, and were sent out to mingle among provincials.
Approaching a Roman city in foreign clothes could get one arrested and interrogated as a spy.

The story of Neilos reminds us not to seek ethnicity exclusively or primarily in textual notions and definitions: for most people it was a function of tangible, audible, or visual attributes, such as headgear. Ethnic distinctions were activated in real time, on the ground, and were not, as they misleadingly appear to us, abstract academic constructs. For people at the time, they verged on being physical.
zh: 无论我们是否把一种隐含的默认罗马性读进这段话，重要的是行省人口——包括孩子——愿意根据头饰或其他显眼的外观特征作族群归类。帝国少数族群处境的不妙迹象是，他们的第一本能是朝外国人扔石头。但这里的要点关乎族群敏感，以及行省人如何从衣着读出族群。拜占庭作者，例如君士坦丁七世皇帝（剪影3），通常提到罗马人的“习俗”，除其他特征外，正是这些习俗把他们定义为一个民族。语言是这样一个特征，服饰是另一个。保加利亚沙皇彼得的一个儿子从罗马宫廷逗留归来，因穿着罗马服装被一名保加利亚边防士兵杀死。
这可能指的是精英宫廷服饰。但另一些故事则涉及社会下层。我们听说波斯人、后来穆斯林派出的间谍“穿得像罗马人”，会说罗马语言，被派出去混入行省人中间。
穿着外国服装接近罗马城市，可能被捕并被当作间谍审讯。
尼洛斯的故事提醒我们，不要专门或主要在文本观念与定义中寻找族群性：对大多数人来说，族群性是通过头饰之类摸得到、听得见或看得见的特征显现出来的。人们当场就会有族群区分。我们容易误以为那只是一种抽象的学术建构，可对当时的人来说，那几乎是有形的。

en: In the fourteenth century, the historian Nikephoros Gregoras complained in his

that during the reign of Andronikos III Palaiologos (1328–1341) everyone, whether they worked in the fields or the palace, wore strange hats: Latin, Serbian, Bulgarian, or Syrian, each according to his taste.

Writing about a later reign, he complained that the same confusion extended to all dress worn by the Romans, such that, from his dress alone “one could no longer tell whether a person was a Roman or belonged to some other

Here too Romans are imagined as one among a crowded field of equivalent, if not equal, ethnic groups or nations, and the borders between the members of the set could be policed by normative concepts regarding what was appropriate for each.
zh: 十四世纪，史学家尼基弗鲁斯·格雷戈拉斯在其《罗马史》中抱怨，安德罗尼库斯三世·巴列奥略（1328–1341年在位）统治期间，人人无论在田间还是宫中劳作，都戴奇怪的帽子：拉丁的、塞尔维亚的、保加利亚的或叙利亚的，各随其好。
写到更晚的一朝时，他抱怨同样的混乱扩展到罗马人穿的所有服饰，以至于单凭衣着“再也分不清一个人是罗马人，还是属于另一个
（genos）”。
这里，罗马人同样被视为众多族群或民族中的一个。各群体可以相提并论，地位却未必平等；关于何种打扮配得上哪一群体的规范，可以用来维护群体间的界线。

en: Ethnicity in the Black Hole
zh: 黑洞中的族群性

en: The snapshots presented above and in Chapter 1 strongly suggest that the Romans of Byzantium were an ethnic (or national) community. The remainder of this chapter and Chapter 3 will confirm this preliminary conclusion by mapping out, both geographically and socially, whom the Roman sources included and whom they excluded from the Roman community. We will pay attention also to the criteria that justified inclusion and exclusion. The factors that we will find, taken together, suggest that the Romans were an ethnic group that demarcated itself against other ethnic groups by roughly the same criteria that are used by modern scholars to discuss ethnicity.
zh: 上面和第一章呈现的剪影强烈暗示，拜占庭的罗马人是一个族群（或民族）共同体。本章余下部分和第三章将通过在地理和社会两个维度上描绘罗马史料把谁纳入、把谁排除出罗马共同体，来确认这一初步结论。我们也会注意证明纳入与排除正当的标准。我们将发现的这些因素合在一起表明，罗马人是一个族群，它用以与其他族群划界的标准，大致就是现代学者讨论族群性时所用的标准。

en: This approach and the conclusions it produces are far removed from the consensus that prevails in the mainstream of Byzantine Studies. But we are justified in disregarding that consensus for two reasons (there are others, but these will suffice). First, ethnicity has never been a topic of focused, systematic, and theoretically informed research in Byzantine Studies. I know of no study that tries to understand the ethnicities of the Byzantine empire in a way that aligns with fields of research in which the study of ethnicity is more advanced. Indeed, there are almost no studies, whether books or articles, that combine the words “ethnicity” and “Byzantium” in their title. Instead, we have only woolly comments made in passing, usually embedded in general surveys of the culture, and they lack both proof and an explicit theoretical framework. Second, these comments tend to be bipolar: while they deny the existence of the Roman people, when it comes to the empire’s ethnic minorities (e.g., Jews, Armenians, Arabs, Turks), they classify them in a naïve, unreconstructed way as “natural” entities. They present us with the implausible picture of a society that had an undefined and nameless majority alongside manifest minorities that can easily be identified and named.
zh: 这一进路及其产生的结论，与拜占庭研究主流中盛行的共识相去甚远。但我们有理由无视那个共识，理由有二（还有别的，但这两个够了）。第一，族群性在拜占庭研究中从未成为聚焦、系统、有理论支撑的研究课题。我不知道有哪项研究试图以与族群研究更先进的领域相一致的方式，研究拜占庭帝国内的各个族群。事实上，几乎没有标题同时包含“族群性”和“拜占庭”两词的研究，无论专著还是论文。我们有的只是顺带作出的含糊评论，通常嵌在文化通论里，既缺乏证明，也缺乏明确的理论框架。第二，这些评论倾向于两极：一方面否认罗马人民的存在，另一方面对帝国的少数族群（如犹太人、亚美尼亚人、阿拉伯人、突厥人）却想当然地沿用旧观念，将它们视为“天然”存在的实体。它们给我们呈现了一幅难以置信的社会图景：一边是没有界定、没有名称的多数，一边却是明明白白、易于识别命名的少数族群。

en: Consider Cyril Mango’s popular introduction,

children: Byzantium: The Empire of New Rome.

en: Mango refers without difficulty to the Slavs, Armenians, and other minorities of the empire, but when he turns to the bulk of the population, he says that it “had been so thoroughly churned up that it is difficult to tell what ethnic groups were living where.”

Let us set aside that Romans are invisible to him, which is typical of the field. What is more revealing is that he seems to recognize a fixed set of preexisting ethnicities that may either be living separately (and so can be identified by name) or they are mixed up. This mixture does not for him raise the possibility of a new ethnicity emerging out of the “churning,” or of a possible loss of a previous ethnicity compensated by the acquisition of a new one (i.e., Armenians ceasing to regard themselves as Armenians and becoming Romans). Instead, churning creates only an epistemological impasse by making it hard to trace the (ideally) separate history of the preapproved real ethnicities. A mixture cannot, in this model, ever result in an ethnicity of its own. Mango imagines the world’s ethnicities as a fixed set that includes Slavs and Armenians (as natural entities that do not need to be problematized) and excludes Romans. No reason is given for this distinction. It has no basis in the primary sources, which treat Armenians and Romans as formally equivalent ethnic categories.
zh: 想想西里尔·曼戈的流行入门书《拜占庭：新罗马的帝国》。曼戈毫无困难地提到帝国的斯拉夫人、亚美尼亚人和其他少数族群，但转到人口主体时，他说它“被搅动得如此彻底，以至于难以分辨哪些族群住在哪里”。

暂且不论罗马人对他不可见——这是本学科的典型。更能说明问题的是，他似乎承认一组固定的既有族群，它们要么分开居住（因而可以按名识别），要么被混在一起。这种混合对他来说并不引出一种新族群从“搅动”中诞生的可能，也没让他想到，人们可能不再归属于旧族群，转而获得新的归属（即亚美尼亚人不再自视为亚美尼亚人而成为罗马人）。相反，在他看来，混合只会使人陷入无法认识的困境，让那些预先已被承认为真实、并且理应彼此分立的族群难以各自追溯其历史。在这个模型里，混合永远不可能产生自己的族群。曼戈把世界诸族群想象为一个固定集合，包含斯拉夫人和亚美尼亚人（视二者为毋须追问如何形成的天然实体），排除罗马人。这一区分没有给出理由。它在第一手史料中没有根据，史料把亚美尼亚人和罗马人当作形式上对等的族群范畴。

en: In reality, all ethnic groups, both those that are on Mango’s radar (Slavs and Armenians) as well as those that are not (Romans), emerge from churning, because there are no “pure” ethnicities. Granted, in 1980, Mango was not familiar with ethnogenesis, the study of how ethnic groups emerge from a fusion of other groups and elements (though, as we saw at the end of Chapter 1, Steven Runciman had in 1929 identified the United States as a nation that lacked a single “ethnological” background). But consider Averil Cameron’s
published in 2006. Cameron states explicitly that the Byzantines were not an ethnic group despite the fact that “they called themselves ‘Romans.’”
Roman ethnicity can be denied without any argumentation,
but Cameron does give a reason, namely that “the population had been thoroughly mixed for many centuries.”

In other words, Cameron does not believe that an ethnic group can have a mixed background, which means that she is unfamiliar with all research about ethnicity since World War II. Like Mango, she intuitively talks about the Slavs, Armenians, and Jews of the empire as ethnic groups, which means she thinks they were unmixed, or pure. It has apparently still not sunk in, by 2006, that every ethnicity is the result of mixture, and that ethnicities are not biological entities but social constructs that emerge, disappear, fuse, and break up. Cameron is likewise operating with a preapproved list of ethnicities, and the Romans are not on it. What the sources treat as the Roman people she sees as an agglomerated jumble of presumably denatured ethnicities. A mess of that kind can have no name, at least not a “real” one.
zh: 实际上，所有族群——无论是曼戈列入考虑的斯拉夫人和亚美尼亚人，还是未纳入考虑的罗马人——都从不同群体的混合中形成，因为没有“纯粹”的族群。诚然，1980年的曼戈还不熟悉族群生成（ethnogenesis），即研究不同群体和要素如何融合成新族群（不过正如我们在第一章末尾所见，史蒂文·朗西曼1929年已把美国认定为一个缺乏单一“族群学”背景的民族）。但看看阿夫里尔·卡梅伦2006年出版的《拜占庭人》。卡梅伦明确说拜占庭人不是一个族群，尽管“他们自称‘罗马人’”。
罗马族群性可以不经任何论证就被否认，
但卡梅伦确实给了一个理由，即“人口已经彻底混合了许多世纪”。

换言之，卡梅伦不相信一个族群可以有混合背景，这意味着她对二战以来所有关于族群性的研究都不熟悉。和曼戈一样，她直觉地把帝国的斯拉夫人、亚美尼亚人和犹太人当作族群来谈论，这意味着她认为他们未混合、或纯粹。到2006年，显然仍未深入人心的是：每个族群都是混合的结果，族群不是生物实体，而是诞生、消失、融合、分裂的社会建构。卡梅伦同样在操作一份预先认可的族群清单，罗马人不在其上。史料里称为罗马人民的群体，在她眼里不过是一堆族群的混杂物，仿佛这些族群已经失掉了原有特性。在她看来，这般混杂的群体不可能有名字，至少没有一个“真正的”名字。

en: Denialists can “see” ethnicities that have a modern equivalent, but “Romans” who lack a modern nation to stick up for them must remain nameless. We thus face the problem of an unidentified majority, which appears as a kind of black hole: in scholarship, it gives off no light of its own, but its shape can be traced in negative by what surrounds it, such as foreign barbarians and internal ethnic minorities. Slavs, Armenians, Jews, and Bulgarians can somehow be seen as distinct from it, but it itself remains nameless. The two problems in this picture of ethnicity and empire are Roman denialism on the one hand and a naive and unreconstructed view of other ethnicities on the other. Chapter 5 will show that some in the field still treat ethnicities as fixed races whose essence is transmitted biologically. Yet a big shift has taken place since the early twentieth century in the study of ethnicity to which Byzantine Studies eventually has to adjust. Some background is necessary.
zh: 否认论者能“看见”有现代对应物的族群，但缺乏现代民族为其撑腰的“罗马人”必须保持无名。于是我们面临一个未识别大多数的问题，它呈现为一种黑洞：在学术中，它自己不发光，它的轮廓只能由周围的事物反衬出来，例如外部的蛮族和帝国内部的少数族群。斯拉夫人、亚美尼亚人、犹太人和保加利亚人不知怎地可以被看作与它不同，但它本身仍无名。这幅族群与帝国图景中的两个问题，一方面是罗马否认论，另一方面是对其他族群不加反省、流于天真的看法。第五章将表明，本学科仍有人把族群当作本质靠生物传递的固定种族。然而自二十世纪初以来，族群研究已发生巨大转变，拜占庭研究终究必须适应。需要一些背景。

en: In the aftermath of World War II, the humanities and social sciences rejected the view that race—or biological traits that are passed on genetically—can determine or explain the cultural, moral, or political makeup of groups and individuals, and therefore their histories and identities (who they think they are). This consensus was codified in a series of statements on the “race concept” that were promulgated after 1950 under the aegis of UNESCO and signed by dozens of leading scientists and scholars. To be sure, the race concept is a potent historical force for societies that believe in it, but scholars have largely recognized that it is a fiction. Instead of seeing history as the interaction of fixed races or immutable nations, scholarship in most fields has turned its attention to the ways in which social forces cause certain groups to coalesce and emerge as historical entities and agents. The concepts of “ethnicity” and “identity” were developed in order to provide a flexible framework for the study of groups that are identified (by themselves or by others) as different from their neighbors in terms of culture or descent (or both). These concepts facilitated a shift from objective to subjective factors. Ethnic differences are seen as historically constructed, not hardwired into groups or individuals. No group is “pure,” as all emerge and evolve through intermarriage with others, by merging, splitting off, and reassimilating, or change their identities in response to circumstances. Seneca wrote that “every day there are names of new nations, and old ones go extinct or are absorbed into more powerful ones . . . all peoples have become confused and mixed up.”
He attained this realization in part because many Romans viewed their own nation as a mixture and melting together of prior ethnic groups.
zh: 二战之后，人文与社会科学拒斥了这样一种观点：种族——或靠基因传递的生物特征——能够决定或解释群体与个人的文化、道德或政治构成，从而决定或解释他们的历史与认同（他们自认为谁）。1950年以后，在联合国教科文组织主持下，几十位著名科学家和学者签署并发表了一系列关于“种族概念”的声明，明确确立了这一共识。诚然，对相信它的社会来说，种族概念是一种强大的历史力量，但学者们大体承认它是虚构。大多数领域的学术不再把历史看作固定种族或不变民族的互动，而把注意力转向各种社会力量如何促使人们凝聚成群体，作为历史上的实体和行动者出现。“族群性”与“认同”概念的发展，是为研究那些（被自己或他人）认定为在文化或世系（或两者）上不同于邻人的群体提供一个灵活框架。这些概念促成了从客观因素到主观因素的转变。族群差异被视为历史建构的，并非群体或个人与生俱来的特质。没有群体是“纯粹”的，因为所有群体都通过与他人的通婚、合并、分裂、再同化而诞生和演变，或随环境改变认同。塞涅卡写道：“每天都有新民族的名字出现，旧的则灭绝或被更强大的吸收……所有民族已经交错混杂。”
他获得这一认识，部分因为许多罗马人把自己的民族视为先前族群的混合与熔合。

en: For example, before the Roman conquest, Italy was populated by many ethnic groups such as the Etruscans who had their own ethnonyms, traditions, polities, languages, and a sense of difference from the Romans and each other. Centuries after the Roman conquest, by contrast, their polities and languages were mostly extinct, and they had become Latin-speaking members of a more expansive Roman state, and no less Roman than anyone else. They had not been biologically replaced with Romans; rather, their culture had changed in ways that made them into Romans. Consider also the inhabitants of Asia Minor, for example the Carians in the southwest. Successive cultural changes transformed them first into Greeks, then into Romans, and later into Turks. It is arbitrary to assume that any one of these phases represents their “essence.” Those who argue that the Byzantines were “really” Greeks and not Romans forget that the Greeks of Asia Minor had not always been Greek. The geographer Strabo said that the Carians were among the first in that land to “try to live in a Greek way and learn our language.”
zh: 例如，罗马征服之前，意大利住着许多族群，如伊特鲁里亚人，他们有自己的族名、传统、政治共同体、语言，以及彼此之间和相对于罗马人的差异感。相比之下，罗马征服数百年后，他们的政治共同体和语言大多灭绝，他们成了地域更广的罗马国家中说拉丁语的成员，是同其他人一样的罗马人。他们并没有在生物意义上被罗马人替换；而是自身的文化发生变化，使他们成了罗马人。再看看小亚细亚的居民，例如西南部的卡里亚人。接连的文化变迁先把他们变成希腊人，再变成罗马人，后来变成突厥人。假定其中任何一个阶段代表他们的“本质”，都是任意的。那些论证拜占庭人“真的”是希腊人而不是罗马人的人忘了，小亚细亚的希腊人并不总是希腊人。地理学家斯特拉波说，卡里亚人是那片土地上最早“尝试按希腊方式生活并学习我们的语言”的人群之一。

en: As ethnic and other identities are social and cultural constructs, a group can change its name and narrative without necessarily receiving an influx of new “blood.” Most scholars accept this thesis, and I suppose most Byzantinists do too, at least in theory.

In practice, however, many continue to think of ethnicity or identity generally as a function of blood, by which presumably they mean genes (the biology is outdated too here). I take it that the primary audience of this book accepts the postwar paradigm and wants to learn how it plays out in the case of Byzantium.
zh: 由于族群与其他认同是社会文化建构，一个群体可以改变自己的名字和叙事，而不必迎来新“血液”的注入。大多数学者接受这一论题，我想大多数拜占庭学家也接受，至少在理论上。
然而在实践中，许多人仍认为族群性乃至一般意义的认同取决于血缘，他们大概指的是基因（这里的生物学也过时了）。我认为本书的主要读者接受战后范式，并想了解它在拜占庭案例中如何展开。

en: Yet Byzantine Studies has not fully made the transition to this postwar model. I will mention two reasons for this failure. First, the field rarely engages with scholarship on ethnicity: from the nineteenth century onward, it displays a continuous tradition of identifying the constituent ethnic groups of the empire in fixed racial or national terms. I discern no rupture in this tradition corresponding to the irruption of newer models. Second, much of this scholarship consists of, or relies on, the national historiographies of modern countries that have ideological stakes in identifying members of their nation in the Byzantine “mix.” Countries that are geographically situated in territories of the empire still promote official historiographies that rely, whether explicitly or in more coded ways, on racial views of the past and these are injected into the international conversation about Byzantium. The stakes for them range from establishing the continuity or purity of the nation to documenting its claim to specific territories and highlighting the greatness of its past. To be fair, these countries did not participate in the excesses of western “scientific race theory” and were not responsible for World War II; in some cases, they were its victims. It would be hypocritical for the west, given its legacy of racism, genocide, colonialism, and slavery, to police the parochial nationalism of Balkan, Turkish, and Caucasian views of history. Still, those views are backed by national institutions that naturalize the diachronic existence of their ancestral groups. By contrast, the Romans of Byzantium lack that advantage
face the sanctions of denialism.
zh: 然而拜占庭研究尚未完全过渡到这个战后模型。我只谈转变尚未完成的两个原因。第一，本学科很少与族群性学术对话：从十九世纪起，它表现出一种持续的传统，即以固定的种族或民族口径认定帝国的构成族群。我没有看到较新的研究模式带来任何足以打破这一传统的转变。第二，这类学术很大一部分由现代国家的民族史学构成、或依赖它们，而这些国家有意识形态上的利害关系，要在拜占庭混杂的人群中辨认出自己的民族成员。地理上位于帝国领土的国家仍在推行官方史学，它们或明或暗地依赖对过去的种族看法，并被注入关于拜占庭的国际对话。它们的利害从确立民族的连续性或纯洁性，到证明其对特定领土的主张、突出其过去的伟大。公平地说，这些国家没有参与西方“科学种族理论”的过度行为，也不对二战负责；有些情况下它们是受害者。鉴于西方种族主义、种族灭绝、殖民主义和奴隶制的遗产，西方若去管制巴尔干、土耳其和高加索历史观的狭隘民族主义，将是虚伪的。尽管如此，那些看法有国家机构撑腰，把其祖先所属群体在各个时代的延续说成自然而然。相比之下，拜占庭的罗马人缺少这种支持，
要承受否认论的排斥。

en: Some basic definitions are necessary at this point to get us up to speed. Ethnic groups are defined by a constellation of factors that converge to produce a unique cultural profile, though groups can always be found that lack one or two of these factors. They include a belief in a shared ancestry and history, a common homeland, language, religion, cultural norms and traditions, and an ethnonym to tie it all together along with a perception of difference from outside groups (who are often viewed negatively or as a threat) and a normative ideal of solidarity in the face of this threat.

There must also be evidence that these components, or indicia of collective identity, are understood by the group as the salient criteria of inclusion and exclusion. The ethnonym typically acts as their lynchpin, as in “the homeland of the Romans,” “the language of the Romans,” and so on for religion, kinship structures, customs, and the like. The argument made in the first part of this book is that the Romans of Byzantium were an ethnic group because they had, and knew that they had, these components of ethnicity. This was not just a matter of passive recognition. There were contexts in which ethnicity spurred a course of action because it situated its bearers within a charged narrative. In the episode from the
that we saw in Snapshot 2, this incitement to action is intriguingly called the “impulse of the
” It incited the second generation of captive Romans to return to the homeland.
zh: 这里先交代几个基本定义。族群由一组因素界定，这些因素共同构成其独有的文化特征，不过总有一些群体缺少其中一两项。这些因素包括相信彼此有共同的祖先和历史，有共同的故土、语言、宗教、文化规范与传统，有一个族名将这些因素联系起来，也包括意识到自己与外部群体有别（往往负面看待他们，或视他们为威胁），以及在面对这种威胁时理当团结的规范观念。

还必须有证据显示，该群体把这些集体认同的要素或标志视为划定成员资格的主要标准。族名往往是将这些标志串在一起的关键，例如“罗马人的故土”“罗马人的语言”，宗教、亲属关系、习俗也概莫能外。本书第一部主张，拜占庭的罗马人之所以是一个族群，是因为他们具有这些族群性的要素，也知道自己具有这些要素。这并非只是被动地承认而已。有些情况下，族群性把人们放进一套情绪充沛的叙事中，由此促使他们采取某种行动。剪影2所引《圣德米特里奥斯圣迹集》里，这种促使人行动的力量被耐人寻味地称作“
（genos）的驱力”。它促使被掳罗马人的子女一代返回故土。

en: The factor on which there is most uncertainty among scholars today is the belief in a common ancestry. Some regard it as paramount for an ethnicity, but most now downplay it in favor of some combination of other elements.

Either way, shared ancestry is understood to be a group belief, not a fact of biology. A society’s myth of descent is malleable and can accommodate the absorption of new groups. For example, people can invent ancestors or choose which aspects of their past to highlight for the purposes of constructing new social identities. As we will see, the Romans of Byzantium referred to their shared ancestry even though they knew that they had absorbed foreigners in large numbers.
zh: 今天，学界最难取得一致的是对共同祖先的信念应占什么位置。有人视它为族群性的首要因素，但大多数人现在淡化它，转而看重其他要素的某种组合。
无论如何，共同祖先被理解为一种群体信念，而非生物学事实。一个社会关于祖裔的神话是可以改变的，可以把新吸收的群体纳入其中。例如，人们可以发明祖先，或为建构新社会认同的目的选择突出过去的哪些方面。我们将会看到，拜占庭的罗马人提到他们的共同祖先，尽管他们知道自己大量吸收了外人。

en: There is considerable overlap between this understanding of ethnicity and conventional definitions of nationality, to the point where some scholars believe that in certain contexts they cannot easily be differentiated.
I think that Byzantium was one such case. In previous publications, I offered a provisional argument that the Romans of Byzantium constituted—and were aware that they constituted—a nation.

This made their state, which they called Romanía, or the state or land of the Romans, into a nation-state. The accumulation of additional evidence and continued study of recent theoretical literature on the existence of premodern nations has convinced me that this model is valid, despite objections that stem from outdated models according to which nations are an exclusively modern phenomenon.
Yet my discussion of ethnicity in those earlier studies adhered to theoretical definitions that I no longer believe are helpful. I therefore wish to modify my position regarding the
of nation that these Romans were.
zh: 这种族群性理解与民族性的常规定义有相当大的重叠，以至于有些学者认为在某些语境中两者不易区分。
我认为拜占庭就是这样一个案例。在先前出版物中，我曾初步提出：拜占庭的罗马人构成——并且意识到自己构成——一个民族。
这使他们的国家——他们称之为罗曼尼亚，即罗马人的国家或土地——成为一个民族国家。更多证据的积累和对前现代民族存在之近期理论文献的持续研究，使我相信这个模型有效，尽管有源自过时模型的反对意见，按那些模型民族是纯粹的现代现象。
然而我在那些早期研究中对族群性的讨论遵循了我不再认为有帮助的理论定义。因此，我想修正自己的立场，重新说明这些罗马人属于
民族。

en: In my previous publications, over ten years ago, I adhered to a model of ethnicity that required a belief in a shared ancestry. Now, the Byzantines, like the ancient Romans, regularly took in foreign groups, gradually absorbed and assimilated them, and were, moreover, aware of the fact that they did so.

Many Byzantine Romans did not hide the fact that they had foreign ancestors. I therefore concluded that the Romans of Byzantium must have constituted a civic nation rather than an ethnic nation. In the former, integrative political structures and a shared culture take the place of ancestry in the core definition of the group. In retrospect, I believe now that I drew too sharp a distinction between ethnic and civic nations and underestimated how often and emphatically the sources point to a kinship-based view of Romanness—the

of the Romans. At the time, I thought that this was just a loose quasi-ethnic way of speaking about what was in reality a civic polity, but I now believe that it was a straightforward expression of ethnic Romanness. My error was in not taking the Romans’ own rhetoric at face value enough and in expecting strict and rigorous thinking on their part about collective ancestry. Ethnicities are, after all, based on subjective perceptions, which do not always respect the facts of history, in this case the fact of ethnic mixture. These Romans were certainly a nation, but they represented themselves as an
nation more than I originally thought.
zh: 十多年前，我曾在著作中采用这样一种族群性模型，认为一个族群必须相信自己有共同的祖先。然而，拜占庭人与古罗马人一样，时常接纳外来的群体，逐渐吸纳、同化他们，自己也清楚这一过程。
许多拜占庭的罗马人不讳言祖辈中有外人。因此我曾推断，拜占庭的罗马人构成的必定是一个公民民族，而非族群民族。界定公民民族的核心是有整合作用的政治结构和共同文化，祖裔并不占那个位置。现在回看，我把族群民族和公民民族分得太截然了，也低估了史料提出血亲意义上的罗马性有多频繁、语气有多明确，换言之，就是罗马人这一
（genos）。我当时以为，人们只是用较为宽泛、近似族群的语言来描述一个实为公民共同体的政体；如今我认为，这就是对族群意义上的罗马性的直接表达。我的错误在于，没有照罗马人自己所说的去充分理解他们的话，却期待他们用严谨而一致的方式思考共同祖先。族群性毕竟建立在主观认识上，这种认识未必顾及历史事实，此处便是各族群发生过混合的事实。这些罗马人当然构成了一个民族，但他们自我表述为
民族的程度超过我先前的估计。

en: Civic nations, it turns out, are just as likely to represent themselves as ethnically defined communities even when they “know” that their ancestry is mixed. As Max Weber suggested, “It is primarily the political community, no matter how artificially organized, that inspires the belief in common ethnicity.”
Such a community can overlook its mixed background in order to represent itself as an ethnicity. In this way, the Romans could represent themselves as a kinship community

a nation. The present book will study this representation under the category of ethnicity, leaving aside the more contested category of the nation, to which I will devote a separate monograph in due course. Even though the two categories are functionally equivalent in this case, as stated above, the literature on the nation tends to focus more on its sustaining institutions. That other book will therefore study the eastern Roman nation as a function of governmentality.
zh: 事实证明，公民民族也同样可能把自己描述为一个由族群归属界定的共同体，即便他们“知道”自己的祖先是混合的。正如马克斯·韦伯所说：“使人相信彼此同属一个族群的，主要是政治共同体，无论这个共同体的组织方式多么人为。”
这样的共同体可以无视自己的混合背景，把自己呈现为一个族群。这样，罗马人就能把自己呈现为一个亲属共同体，
也是一个民族。本书将在族群性范畴下研究这种呈现，把更有争议的民族范畴搁置一旁，我会在适当时候另写一部专著讨论它。尽管如上所述两个范畴在此案例中功能上对等，关于民族的研究往往更关注维系民族的制度。因此，那部另写的书将把东部罗马民族作为治理性（governmentality）的产物来考察。

en: My argument for a Roman ethnicity will focus on the middle Byzantine period while occasionally linking up to the early and later periods. It should be noted, however, that the later Byzantine period has had a somewhat different reception in the scholarship, as it is discussed more casually in ethnic terms. The reason for this is that in the later period Byzantium was visited—or inundated—by westerners who may have called the Romans “Greeks” but regarded them unambiguously as an ethnic group. Consider a Latin account of Constantinople, probably from the later eleventh century. It says that the City contained many
—Greeks, Armenians, Syrians, Lombards, English, Dacians, Amalfitans, and Franks—but the Greeks occupied the largest and best part of the City.

The medieval sources viewed these Greeks as having their own customs, language, homeland, ancient ancestors, and faith—the components of an ethnicity. Apart from the label and its derogatory uses in western sources, the Byzantine Romans would have agreed. Thus, as it is easy for western scholars to follow the lead of western sources, discussions of the later period tend to ethnicize the Byzantines more, albeit at the cost of calling them “Greeks.” It is hard to decide whether this misreading is better than the field’s denialism: it gets the analytical category right, even if it does so for the wrong reason and so mislabels it with the wrong name.
zh: 我关于罗马族群性的论证将聚焦拜占庭中期，偶尔联系早期和晚期。但应注意，史学界对拜占庭晚期的看法有所不同，谈到这一时期时，更习惯使用族群的概念。原因是晚期拜占庭被西方人访问——或淹没——他们可能称罗马人为“希腊人”，但毫不含糊地把他们视为一个族群。想想一份大概出自十一世纪后期的拉丁语君士坦丁堡记述。它说城中有许多gentes（族群）——希腊人、亚美尼亚人、叙利亚人、伦巴第人、英格兰人、达契亚人、阿马尔菲人和法兰克人——但希腊人占据城中最大最好的部分。
中世纪史料视这些希腊人为有自己的习俗、语言、故土、古代祖先和信仰——族群性的成分。除了标签及其在西方史料中的贬义用法，拜占庭罗马人会同意。于是，由于西方学者容易跟随西方史料的指引，晚期讨论倾向于更常把拜占庭人当作一个族群来谈，尽管代价是称他们为“希腊人”。很难判断这种误读是否比本学科的否认论好：它把分析范畴弄对了，尽管理由有误，也因此用错了族名。

en: Honorable mention goes here to Gill Page’s 2008 book
Based on the unambiguous testimony of the sources, Page saw that ethnicity was a core aspect of Byzantine
though at times she presents it as a phase of being Greek, for example in the subtitle (
earning the book a translation into modern Greek).

Setting that glitch aside, she uses a modern understanding of ethnicity to study the evolution of the Roman ethnic group in the chaos of the post-1204 world. And yet, for all that the book is cited often, its core reading of Roman ethnicity has had little impact on the field. For example, no one has set out to ascertain whether the model works for the period before 1204 (it does).

In this connection, it is curious that, when they reach the period after about 1200, even staunch denialists admit that “the Byzantines” suddenly acquired an ethnic identity, though even then they do not always tell us its name. Nor do they tell us how this ethnogenesis happened. In the course of a page, we can go from a multiethnic Byzantium with an artificial, purely nominal Roman identity, to a Byzantium with a dominant (but unnamed) ethnic identity, and the prior insistence on multiethnicity vanishes.

In reality, no substantive change took place. We need to balance out our views of the culture before and after 1204. The capture of Constantinople by the crusaders intensified preexisting traits in some contexts and weakened them in others, but it did not bring a new people into being.
zh: 这里尤其值得一提的是吉尔·佩奇2008年的书《做拜占庭人》（Being Byzantine）。基于史料的明白证词，佩奇看到族群性是拜占庭罗马性的核心面向，尽管她有时仍把它写成希腊人认同历程的一个阶段，例如在副标题中（《奥斯曼人之前的希腊认同》，这使该书被译成现代希腊语）。
撇开这一点，她用现代族群性理解研究1204年后混乱世界中罗马族群的演变。然而尽管该书被频繁引用，其对罗马族群性的核心解读对本学科影响甚微。例如，没有人着手确认这个模型是否适用于1204年之前的时期（适用）。
与此相关，奇怪的是，当写到约1200年之后的时期时，连坚定的否认论者也承认“拜占庭人”突然获得了一种族群认同，尽管即便如此他们也不总告诉我们它的名字。他们也不解释这一族群是如何形成的。在一页之内，我们可以从一个罗马认同出于人为、徒具名义的多族群拜占庭，读到一个存在主导族群认同（却没有族名）的拜占庭，而先前对多族群性的坚持消失了。
实际上没有发生实质变化。我们需要平衡对1204年前后文化的看法。十字军攻占君士坦丁堡在某些语境中强化了既有特征，在另一些语境中削弱了它们，但没有催生一个新民族。

en: What, then, is the methodology for establishing the historical existence of a premodern ethnic group? The strongest arguments work through discursive evidence, that is, claims that

person or group belonged to this ethnicity because of such and such criterion. It is sometimes argued that the existence of an ethnic group can be established only through such evidence. Ethnicity can be expressed through material culture or physical descriptors, but without the ethnonyms and discursive claims to them it is difficult to know whether an ethnicity existed in the first place to which the material evidence can be attached.
In our case, Roman denialism has blocked the archaeological study of

Byzantium, so we must begin from the written sources and defer the material evidence for now. As it happens, Byzantine sources do occasionally offer approximate definitions of Romanness by listing its main elements, and these suggest strongly that it was an ethnicity (see, e.g., Snapshots 2, 3, 6, and 7). The authors of those texts were able to do this in part because the categories of ancient ethnography were similar to those used by modern scholars, and in part because they could observe firsthand what made Romans distinct.
zh: 那么，确立一个前现代族群历史存在的方法论是什么？最有力的论证凭借话语证据，也就是指出
人或群体依据某项标准属于某个族群的说法。有时有人论证，一个族群的存在只能通过这种证据确立。族群性可以通过物质文化或体貌描述表达，但如果既不知道族名，也没有采用这些族名的文字表述，就很难确定是否存在一个与这些物质证据对应的族群。
在我们的案例中，罗马否认论阻碍了对拜占庭
的考古研究，所以我们必须从文字史料开始，暂且搁置物质证据。碰巧，拜占庭史料确实偶尔通过列举罗马性的主要要素给出近似定义，而这些强烈暗示它是一种族群性（参见如剪影2、3、6、7）。那些文本的作者之所以能这样做，部分因为古代民族志的范畴与现代学者所用相似，部分因为他们能直接观察是什么使罗马人独特。

en: These are useful texts, but we do not need to rely exclusively on them. Roman claims in Byzantine literature are abundant and come from a wide range of authors, writing in many geographical locations, social contexts, genres, and linguistic registers. They are extraordinarily consistent in the picture that they paint of the Roman community. The criteria for belonging to this community were not being continually reinvented along radically different axes in different periods, nor were they fiercely being contested among different constituencies within Romanía, as has recently been argued, for example, about early Frankish identity.
To be sure, Byzantine Romanness had its own history of change and evolution that remains to be told, but it was one of shifting nuance and emphasis; the general framework remained stable.
zh: 这些是有用的文本，但我们不必只依赖它们。拜占庭文献中关于罗马身份的说法比比皆是，出自许多作者，跨越不同地区、社会语境、文体和语域。它们描绘的罗马共同体图景惊人地一致。归属这个共同体的标准并没有随时代更迭而反复改用截然不同的原则来规定，也没有像最近有人论证早期法兰克认同时所说的那样，在罗曼尼亚内部不同群体之间激烈争夺。
诚然，拜占庭罗马性有自己的变化演变史有待讲述，但那是细微差别与重点转移的历史；总体框架保持稳定。

en: What we need at first, then, are general “maps” of who was included and who excluded from the Roman community, in order to establish its contours. When we then scrutinize the grounds for such inclusion and exclusion, between the sixth and the thirteenth centuries, we find that they correspond closely to the requirements of an ethnicity, as set by modern theoretical definitions. In this way we will triangulate the coordinates of Byzantine Romanness by using multiple texts and points of view. In the next section we will consider

made the relevant claims on which the analysis rests, to ensure that we are not adopting the perspective of a narrow group that may have had an interested reason to project a distorted view. Fortunately, this is not so, and we do not even need to rely exclusively on Byzantine sources to make the case. Arabic sources will be used to reinforce the picture painted by the Byzantines.
zh: 因此我们首先需要的是关于谁被纳入、谁被排除出罗马共同体的一般“地图”，以确立其轮廓。当我们随后审视六至十三世纪这种纳入与排除的根据时，发现它们与现代理论定义所设的族群性要求紧密对应。这样我们将把多种文本和观点放在一起交叉印证，从不同角度确定拜占庭罗马性的范围。下一节我们将查明本项分析所用的这些说法都是
提出的，以免不自觉地采纳某一狭小群体的视角，而那个群体可能出于自身利益歪曲现实。幸运的是并非如此，我们甚至不必只依赖拜占庭史料来立案。阿拉伯史料将用来强化拜占庭人描绘的图景。

en: A word, finally, on the Greek words
and
It is correct and expected to say that they do not always correspond to the modern concepts of race, ethnic group, tribe, or nation, even though sometimes they do.
These terms are used loosely in texts to refer to different kinds of groups, no matter how they are constituted, so we might read about the
of locusts, women, philosophers, or Christians. But in the relevant context and the right kind of text, they often bear senses that approximate to notions of race, ethnicity, nation, or kinship.

in particular refers literally to a person’s birth and can establish an ethnic claim. Therefore, while we should not rely absolutely on these terms to establish a thesis about ethnicity, we should not deny that in the right discursive context they reflect a roughly equivalent concept. Again, we do not have to accept the Byzantines’ claim that they, as Romans, were all related to each other. But we have to recognize that their profession of this belief qualifies them to be counted as an ethnic group. The argument will therefore not be philological but based on the presence of the substantive components of ethnicity in Byzantine society and its self-representation.
zh: 最后说说希腊语的
和
。指出这些词并不总与现代所谓的种族、族群、部族或民族相对应，是正确的，也不出所料，尽管有时两者确实相合。
文本里用这些词的范围很宽，可以指各式各样的群体，无论它们是如何构成的。因此，我们可能读到蝗虫的
、妇女的
、哲学家的
，也可能读到基督徒的
。但在相应语境和相应类型的文本里，这些词常有接近种族、族群性、民族或亲缘关系的意思。尤其是
，它直接指人的出身，可以据此主张自己属于某个族群。因此，我们既不应完全凭这几个词来证明关于族群性的判断，也不能否认它们在适当的话语语境里表达了大致相当的概念。同理，拜占庭人说他们作为罗马人都彼此有亲缘关系，我们无须信为事实。但必须看到，他们明言相信这件事，自己就可因此被视为一个族群。所以，下面的论证并不依赖语文学，而要看拜占庭社会及其自我表述中是否有组成族群性的实质要素。

en: Who Was Included?
zh: 谁被纳入？

en: In 212, the
made almost all free people in the empire Roman citizens.
The principle was subsequently enshrined in Roman law, for instance in the
of Justinian, that “all who are in the Roman world are Roman citizens.” This was translated into Greek in the
the Byzantine version of the

that was made into law in the late ninth century, to which an interesting scholion was appended that reflected the transition between a world ruled by the Romans and a world in which all were Romans: “Those who live within the circumference of the Roman world, namely those who are under the authority of the Romans, even if they do not live in Rome, are still Roman citizens on the basis of the decree issued by the emperor Antoninus.”
This legal criterion of Romanness excluded slaves and some barbarian groups who entered imperial territory after the
zh: 212年，《安东尼努斯敕令》（Constitutio Antoniniana）使帝国几乎所有自由人成为罗马公民。

这一原则随后被载入罗马法，例如查士丁尼《民法大全》（Corpus）中的“凡在罗马世界之内者皆为罗马公民”。九世纪后期，《民法大全》的拜占庭版本《巴西尔法典》（Basilika）颁行为法律。这条原则在该法典中以希腊语写成，并附有一条有意思的古注，反映了从罗马人统治的世界到人人皆罗马人的世界之间的过渡：“凡居住在罗马世界范围之内者，即在罗马人权威之下者，即使不住在罗马城，依安东尼努斯皇帝颁布的敕令，仍是罗马公民。”
这一罗马性的法律标准排除了奴隶，以及《敕令》之后进入帝国领土的某些蛮族群体。

en: In looking for Romans, citizenship is a place to start, but many scholars of the later empire do not find legal definitions to be, in themselves, compelling. It is conventional to say that Roman citizenship became effectively irrelevant when it was extended to everyone, that it remained in the background where no one really noticed it or cared about it, except for a few jurists. While this issue is not my primary focus here, the assumption is not necessarily correct. For example, the universal grant of citizenship shaped the rulers’ perceptions of the empire and its subjects, affecting the very nature of governance. As Caesar in Gaul in the 350s, Julian reminded his cousin, Constantius II, that “no matter where they are born, all [subjects of the empire] partake of Rome’s constitution, use the laws and customs that were promulgated from there, and by virtue of these facts are its citizens.”

As we will discuss in the second half of this book, “empire” and relations of imperial domination represent the rule of one ethnic group, nation, or religious community over a number of other groups who are understood by the ruling group to be different. When all became Romans, even if only legally, Rome ceased to be an empire and became something else, whose precise nature remains to be explored. Studies of late Roman imperial rhetoric and ideology have documented a shift from an empire of conquest, in which non-Romans were the “slaves” of their Roman masters, to a global state beaming universal solicitude to all subjects. Emperors presented themselves “as populist monarchs whose care extended not merely to privileged groups of imperial citizens but to
their subjects.”
zh: 寻找罗马人时，公民身份是一个起点，但许多研究后期帝国的学者认为法律定义本身并不令人信服。通常的说法是，罗马公民身份扩展到所有人时就实际上变得无关紧要了，它退居背景，除了少数法学家没人真正注意或在乎。虽然这个问题不是我这里的主要焦点，但这个假设未必正确。例如，公民身份的普遍授予塑造了统治者对帝国及其臣民的看法，影响了治理本身的性质。350年代在高卢任恺撒时，尤利安提醒他的堂兄君士坦提乌斯二世：“无论出生在哪里，所有［帝国臣民］都参与罗马的政制，遵循自罗马颁行的法律与习俗，并因此成为罗马的公民。”

正如本书后半部分将讨论的，“帝国”与帝国支配关系代表一个族群、民族或宗教共同体对若干其他群体的统治，而统治集团认为这些被统治者与自己有别。当所有人都成为罗马人时——哪怕只在法律上——罗马就不再是帝国，而成了别的什么东西，其确切性质有待探索。对晚期罗马帝国修辞与意识形态的研究记录了一种转变：从征服帝国（其中非罗马人是其罗马主人的“奴隶”）转向一个宣称一视同仁地关怀所有臣民的世界性国家。皇帝让自己显得“是亲民的君主，他们关心的不仅是帝国公民中的特权群体，还有自己的
臣民”。

en: Nor did universal citizenship necessarily remain a legal concept that only certain high-placed functionaries of the state knew or cared about. Discussing St. Paul’s claim to Roman citizenship in Acts of the Apostles 22:25, John Chrysostom reminded his congregation that “those who held that honor in that era enjoyed great privileges, and not everyone held it. They say that everyone was made a Roman under Hadrian, but formerly it was not so.”

We can draw a mixed set of conclusions from this: Chrysostom confirms that Roman citizenship was, indeed, no big deal in his own time since everyone had it, but he also reveals that his audience did in fact know that they were Roman citizens and perhaps imagined that universal citizenship had always been the case in the empire, prompting his historical commentary.
zh: 普遍公民身份也未必只是一个只有某些国家高级官员知道或在乎的法律概念。讨论《使徒行传》22:25中圣保罗对罗马公民身份的主张时，金口约翰提醒他的会众：“那个时代拥有此荣誉者享有极大特权，并非人人都有。他们说哈德良治下人人都成了罗马人，但从前并非如此。”
这提示了两个不同的结论。金口约翰的确表明罗马公民身份在他自己的时代确实不算什么，因为人人都有；但他也透露，他的听众事实上知道自己是罗马公民，或许还以为帝国从来人人都有公民身份，这才有了他这番历史说明。

en: The argument of this book that the Byzantines knew themselves to be Romans will not take its stand on citizenship. Victory in that battle would be swift and decisive, but the spoils would be meager without a deeper analysis of Roman governmentality. I believe that Byzantine society was structured on a fundamental level by Roman legal concepts and their ongoing modulation by the state. But that would take us in a different direction. A legal definition tells us little about ethnicity. For example, we saw in Snapshot 1 how Isaurians in the fifth century were regarded as a separate ethnicity even though they were Roman citizens of the empire. One might theoretically imagine that a multiethnic agglomeration of peoples, marked by diversity of culture, ethnicity, religion, and language, could coexist beneath the formal umbrella of Roman citizenship. This is, in fact, what many scholars of Byzantium believe. Thus, we must demonstrate more than a legal homogeneity for the majority Roman population. Inclusion and exclusion—Roman and non-Roman—were defined and perceived in Byzantium primarily on ethnic grounds, not legal ones. So let us sketch the contours of the Roman community, geographically and socially.
zh: 本书关于拜占庭人自知为罗马人的论证不会立足于公民身份。那场战斗的胜利会迅速而决定性，但若无对罗马治理性的更深分析，战利品将很微薄。我相信拜占庭社会在根本层面上由罗马法律概念及国家对这些概念的持续调整塑造。但那会把我们带向不同方向。单凭法律定义，很少能说明族群性问题。例如，我们在剪影1看到，五世纪的伊苏里亚人虽为帝国罗马公民，仍被视为一个独立族群。理论上可以想象，文化、族群、宗教和语言各异的人群，可以在形式上同为罗马公民。事实上这正是许多拜占庭研究者的信念。因此，我们必须证明，占人口多数的罗马人除了具有同样的法律身份，还具有更多共同之处。纳入与排除——罗马与非罗马——在拜占庭主要按族群而非法律根据来定义和感知。那么让我们在地理和社会两个维度勾勒罗马共同体的轮廓。

en: Certainly, the majority of the population of Constantinople were Romans and regarded themselves to be such. One could cite hundreds of passages from texts of all kinds that refer to the Roman “people” (i.e.,

) of the capital. We have seen the people’s collective demand that the empress Ariadne appoint, in 491, a true Roman to the throne (Snapshot 1). I limit myself to one more such text, which has the advantage of recording, or claiming to record, the people’s own collective expression of being Roman. The

compiled in the tenth century, records and prescribes the acclamations and antiphonal chants that were to be uttered by the people of Constantinople, the imperial herald, and the representatives of the teams before the races. Among the many things to be said at such occasions, the emperors are called “the beloved of the Romans” and “the joy of the Romans.”
zh: 当然，君士坦丁堡人口的大多数是罗马人，并自视为罗马人。可以从各类文本中引用数百段提到都城罗马“人民”（即populus）的文字。我们已经看到491年人民集体要求皇后阿里阿德涅任命一个真正的罗马人登位（剪影1）。我只再限引一段这样的文本，它的优点是记录了——或声称记录了——人民自己关于做罗马人的集体表达。十世纪编纂的《礼仪之书》记录并规定了君士坦丁堡人民、皇帝的传令官和战车竞赛各队代表在赛前应喊出的欢呼和交替应答的唱词。在这种场合要说的许多话中，皇帝被称为“罗马人之所爱”和“罗马人之喜乐”。

en: The majority of the provincial population are also clearly called Romans in the sources. As many of the sources recount military history, these Romans often appear in accounts of barbarian raids, in which provincials living by the frontier are captured. For example, Prokopios (sixth century) says that “the Gepids held the city of Sirmium and almost all the cities of Dacia . . . and enslaved the Romans of that region.”
Likewise, when the Slavs raided Thrace, they enslaved many of the Romans there, one of whom, apparently an average person, Prokopios calls “a Roman man” in the singular.

He also tries to calculate the total number of the Roman victims of the barbarian raids in the Balkans under Justinian: “More than twenty times ten thousand of the Romans who lived there were either killed or enslaved.”

This was an exaggeration, but it means that Prokopios and his readers found nothing incongruous in the notion that there were hundreds of thousands of Romans in one set of provinces. As these were only the victims, the total population of provincial Romans would have been imagined as much bigger. Theophylaktos Simokattes (seventh century) claims that Slavic raiders carried away “a great haul of captive Romans” from provincial towns in the Balkans.
The historian and later patriarch Nikephoros (eighth century) notes that provincial “Romans” in Asia Minor were captured by invading Persians.

Jumping ahead to a later period, the Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan (d. 1207) styled himself “the Roman-Slayer (Ῥωμαιοκτόνος)” in imitation of the Roman emperor Basileios II, the Bulgar-Slayer. The thirteenth-century historian who tells us this, Georgios Akropolites, says that the tsar took on the name after destroying many cities in Thrace and capturing or killing their Roman inhabitants.
In such texts, the provincials are casually assumed to be Romans.
zh: 行省人口的大多数在史料中也明确被称为罗马人。由于许多史料讲述军事史，这些罗马人常出现在蛮族袭掠的记述中，住在边境的行省人被掳。例如，普罗科匹厄斯（六世纪）说：“格皮德人占有西尔米乌姆城和几乎达契亚的所有城市……并奴役了那个地区的罗马人。”
同样，斯拉夫人袭掠色雷斯时奴役了当地许多罗马人，其中一个显然是普通人，普罗科匹厄斯用单数称他为“一个罗马男人”。
他还试图计算查士丁尼治下巴尔干蛮族袭掠中罗马受害者的总数：“住在那里的罗马人，被杀或沦为奴隶者超过二十万。”
这是夸张，但它意味着普罗科匹厄斯及其读者并不觉得几个行省里居住着数十万罗马人有何奇怪。由于这些只是受害者，行省罗马人的总人口会被想象为大得多。塞奥菲拉克托斯·西莫卡特斯（七世纪）声称，斯拉夫袭掠者从巴尔干行省城镇掳走“大批罗马俘虏”。
史学家、后来的牧首尼基弗鲁斯（八世纪）记载，小亚细亚的行省“罗马人”被入侵的波斯人掳走。
跳到更晚的时期，保加利亚沙皇卡洛扬（卒于1207年）模仿罗马皇帝“保加利亚人屠夫”瓦西里二世，自称“罗马人屠夫（Ῥωμαιοκτόνος）”。告诉我们此事的十三世纪史学家乔治·阿克罗波利特斯说，沙皇是在摧毁色雷斯许多城市、掳杀其罗马居民之后取这个名字的。
在这类文本中，行省居民被视为罗马人，是不言而喻的。

en: These historians refer to provincial Romans in other contexts too, not just military. In a geographical digression on Lazike (Kolchis), Prokopios reaches the border between that non-Roman land and the empire and says that “Romans live in the adjacent land, whom people also qualify as Pontians.”
In other words, their Romanness was primary and their provincial identity (as inhabitants of the province of Pontos) was a qualification of it: they were the Romans of Pontos. In the

Prokopios refers often to the Roman victims of Justinian, and calls them a race: “No Roman man” managed to escape from that emperor, whose evil “fell upon the entire race (ὅλῳ τῷ γένει).” Elsewhere Prokopios refers to Romans “who lived in distant lands,” including “in the countryside.”

Prokopios’ continuer Agathias refers to the (ancient) Pelasgian ethnic origin of the people of the city of Tralleis in Asia Minor, “yet,” he adds, “the townspeople (ἀστοὶ) should not now be called Pelasgians but rather Romans.” This was a case of “Romanogenesis”: turning Pelasgians into Romans. This claim could be made only if “Roman” was understood as categorically equivalent to the previous ethnic label of the population.
zh: 这些史学家也在其他语境、不只是军事语境中提到行省罗马人。在一段关于拉齐凯（科尔基斯）的地理插叙中，普罗科匹厄斯谈到那片非罗马领土与帝国的边界，说：“相邻土地住着罗马人，人们也称他们为本都人。”
换言之，他们的罗马性是首要的，行省认同（作为本都省居民）是用来说明他们是哪个地方的罗马人：他们是本都的罗马人。在《秘史》中，普罗科匹厄斯常提到查士丁尼的罗马受害者，并称他们为一个种族：“没有一个罗马男人”能逃过那个皇帝，其邪恶“降临于整个种族（ὅλῳ τῷ γένει）”。别处普罗科匹厄斯提到“住在遥远土地”、包括“在乡下”的罗马人。
普罗科匹厄斯的续作者阿加提阿斯提到小亚细亚特拉勒斯城人民的（古代）佩拉斯吉族群起源，“然而，”他补充说，“城镇居民（ἀστοὶ）现在不应被称为佩拉斯吉人，而应被称为罗马人。”这是一个“罗马族源生成”的案例：把佩拉斯吉人变成罗马人。只有当“罗马”被理解为与该人口先前族群标签范畴对等时，才能作出这样的主张。

en: Romans were assumed to live in the provinces during the middle period too. For example, the eleventh-century historian Attaleiates commented that the elephant paraded in the capital by Konstantinos IX Monomachos (1042–1055) delighted “the Byzantioi [i.e., Constantinopolitans] and the other Romans who happened to see it,” the latter logically being Romans not from the capital, like Attaleiates himself (who was from Attaleia).
zh: 拜占庭中期，罗马人也住在行省，这一点同样被视为理所当然。例如，十一世纪史学家阿塔雷阿特斯评论说，君士坦丁九世·莫诺马科斯（1042–1055年在位）在都城游行展示的大象使“拜占庭城人（
）［即君士坦丁堡人］和其他碰巧看到它的罗马人”欣喜，后者按逻辑应是像阿塔雷阿特斯本人（他来自阿塔雷亚）那样非出自都城的罗马人。

en: The ethnonym was not limited to provincial

as opposed to women. In the 830s the emperor Theophilos admitted thousands of Khurramite (Iranian) warriors into the empire. In order to integrate them, the emperor enrolled them in the army and “arranged for them to marry Roman women” in the provinces where they were settled. The historians who report this must have assumed that there were thousands of Roman women of marriageable age in the provinces, and we will meet one of them in Chapter 4.
Moreover, in Snapshot 4 we examined the reasoning of Manuel Komnenos, who imagined the totality of the Roman population as a network of kinship associations, obviously including the women too.
zh: 这个族名既适用于行省的男人，也适用于行省的女人。830年代，狄奥斐卢斯皇帝接纳数千胡拉米派（伊朗）战士进入帝国。为整合他们，皇帝把他们编入军队，并“安排他们在定居的行省娶罗马女人为妻”。报道此事的史学家必定假定行省有数千适婚罗马女人，第4章就会谈到其中一人。
此外，剪影4中我们考察了曼努埃尔·科穆宁的推理，他把罗马人口总体想象为一个亲属关系网络，显然也包括女人。

en: The ethnonym was not limited to people of a certain class or occupation. An icon-painting monk of the ninth century was called “one of our Romans” and “a Roman by
” when that monk was requested by the Bulgarian king.

In the thirteenth century, the emperor Ioannes III Doukas Batatzes wanted to reduce his trade deficit and ordered that his subjects were to buy “clothes produced only from the Roman land and by the hands of Romans”—the latter are here textile workers, likely women.

The Romans who appear most frequently in narrative sources, given their emphasis on war, are soldiers. They are called Romans by the historians and addressed as such in direct speech by their officers. These speeches are reported by the historians, who may be suspected of embellishing them with patriotic Roman sentiment. But it is impossible to believe that they simply made up an attribution of Roman pride to the soldiers of the empire and kept this pretense up for a thousand years. The military manuals actually instruct generals to address their soldiers in the following way: “Roman men, let us stand firm and unyielding.”
Konstantinos VII sent a speech in 958 to be read aloud to the army and it addresses them as Romans too.

The soldiers themselves took obvious pride in this name. In some episodes, they are shown begging their commanders to let them fight “so that they could show themselves to be worthy of the name Romans.”
There is no good reason to suspect literary artifice.
zh: 族名不限于特定阶级或职业的人。九世纪一位画圣像的修士被称为“我们罗马人中的一个”和“按
（genos）是罗马人”，当时保加利亚国王索要这位修士。
十三世纪，约翰三世·杜卡斯·瓦塔特泽斯皇帝想减少贸易逆差，下令臣民只买“只在罗马土地上由罗马人亲手制作的衣服”——后者这里是纺织工人，很可能是女人。
鉴于叙事史料侧重战争，其中最常出现的罗马人是士兵。史学家称他们为罗马人，军官在直接引语中也这样称呼他们。记载这些演说的是历史学家，或许会掺进一些罗马爱国情怀加以润饰。但不可能相信他们只是凭空给帝国士兵安上罗马自豪感，并把这种伪装维持了一千年。军事手册实际指示将军们这样对士兵讲话：“罗马人，坚守阵地，绝不退让。”
君士坦丁七世958年送去一篇向军队宣读的演说，也称呼他们为罗马人。
士兵自己显然以这个名字为荣。有些情节中，他们恳求指挥官让他们作战，“以便证明自己配得上罗马人这个名字”。
没有好理由怀疑这是文学手法。

en: To be sure, soldiers were agents of the Roman state and were extensions of the emperors’ will, so the emphasis on their Romanness in this context does have a formal, institutional aspect. But it was not limited to that. In the middle period, most of the soldiers were recruited and stationed in the provinces, and their concerns as soldiers reflected, to a considerable degree, the concerns of their families and local communities.

The financing of their service involved many people in their upkeep and support, which later resulted in legal arrangements and land classifications. If the army rosters of the middle period listed between one and two hundred thousand men, and if we assume that each was supported by a farm or family unit of between four and six people (at least), this means that between half a million to a million provincials were tied to the arrangements that the state made for soldiers, whom our sources emphatically and consistently call Romans. They were the protectors of the provincials whom our sources also call Romans, as we saw above.
zh: 诚然，士兵为罗马国家效力，也是执行皇帝意志的人，所以这个语境中对他们罗马性的强调确有形式、制度的一面。但不限于此。中期大多数士兵在行省征募和驻扎，他们作为士兵的关切在相当程度上反映了其家庭和地方社区的关切。
士兵服役需由许多人提供资助和供养，后来还为此形成相应的法律安排和土地分类。如果中期军队名册列有十至二十万人，并假定每人由一个四至六人（至少）的农场或家庭单位供养，这意味着五十万至一百万行省人与国家为士兵所作的安排绑定在一起，而我们的史料强调且一贯地称这些士兵为罗马人。他们是行省人的保护者，而我们的史料也称行省人为罗马人，如上所见。

en: Economically too Romans could be found at all levels compatible with legal freedom. Consider a decree of Nikephoros III Botaneiates (1078–1081) that is reported by the contemporary historian Attaleiates. That emperor released from certain debts to the imperial fisc “all Romans, wherever on earth they lived, and thereby made them into free Roman citizens.”

The theory behind the passage is that debt is a form of slavery, but what interests us here is the implication that the Roman community was geographically expansive and also included people who were close to insolvency, or actually in that state: they were on the verge of slavery, but the emperor made them “free Romans” again.

This is a case where Romanness is inflected by citizenship in that it concerns a relationship mediated by law, whose purpose is to restore the perks of freedom. The historian Ioannes Kinnamos (twelfth century) likewise recorded how the emperor Manuel I Komnenos (1143–1180) prevented Romans from taking out loans by positing their freedom as collateral, for he “wanted to rule over free Romans, not slaves.”
Romans could therefore be quite poor, but one step above legal slavery.
zh: 经济上，罗马人也存在于与法律自由相容的所有层级。想想同时代史学家阿塔雷阿特斯报道的尼基弗鲁斯三世·波塔尼阿特斯（1078–1081年在位）的一道敕令。那位皇帝免除了“所有罗马人，无论住在世上何处”对帝国国库的某些债务，“从而使他们成为自由的罗马公民”。
这段话背后的理论是债务是一种奴隶制，但我们这里感兴趣的是它的暗示：罗马共同体在地理上是广阔的，也包括接近破产或实际处于那种状态的人：他们濒临奴隶制，但皇帝使他们重新成为“自由罗马人”。
这里的罗马性有公民身份的意涵，因为此事涉及由法律规范的人际关系，旨在让人重新享有自由身份带来的权利。史学家约翰·金纳莫斯（十二世纪）同样记载，曼努埃尔一世·科穆宁皇帝（1143–1180年在位）禁止罗马人以自由作抵押借贷，因为他“想统治自由罗马人，而不是奴隶”。
因此罗马人可以相当穷，但也可能只差一步就在法律上沦为奴隶。

en: In fact, we have some documents of manumission from Byzantium. Two of these from the eleventh century and one from the twelfth state that when the slaves are freed they become “free Roman citizens.”

These new Romans would occupy the bottom of the social scale, thus the salient distinction between Roman and non-Roman was between free and slave, not elite and nonelite. Moreover, based on these texts we can say that the language of citizenship and freedom was not limited to Constantinople because one of these cases is from southern Italy and the other from the eastern reaches of Asia Minor; the third, from the twelfth century, is from Thessalonike or Constantinople.
zh: 事实上，我们有一些拜占庭的释奴文书。其中两份十一世纪、一份十二世纪的文书说，奴隶被释放时成为“自由罗马公民”。
这些新成为罗马人的获释者会处于社会底层，因此罗马与非罗马之间的显著区分是自由与奴隶之间，而非精英与非精英之间。此外，基于这些文本我们可以说，关于公民身份和自由的说法不限于君士坦丁堡，因为其中一个案例来自意大利南部，另一个来自小亚细亚东部边缘；第三个十二世纪的来自塞萨洛尼基或君士坦丁堡。

en: We do not, then, find Romans only or even primarily in Constantinople, as is sometimes asserted. There is no evidence that the Romans of the capital were more Roman than those of the provinces.

Being Roman had nothing to do with social or economic class, occupation, or gender. There were poor Romans, rich Romans, freedmen Romans, soldier Romans, and icon-painter Romans. The legal aspects of Roman citizenship were not especially prominent in constituting this community, although they did occasionally come into play. In sum, the size and shape of the Roman community was that of an ethnic group or nation.
zh: 因此，我们并非只在、甚至主要在君士坦丁堡找到罗马人，尽管有时有人这样断言。没有证据表明都城的罗马人比行省的更罗马。
罗马人身份与社会或经济阶层、职业或性别无关。他们有穷人，也有富人，有获释的奴隶、士兵，也有绘制圣像的人。罗马公民身份的法律面向在构成这个共同体时并不特别突出，尽管偶尔确实起作用。总之，罗马共同体的规模和构成符合一个族群或民族的特征。

en: Who Was Excluded?
zh: 谁被排除？

en: Rather than a scarcity of Romans, we may now face the embarrassment of too many Romans. Some historians believe that everyone living within the empire or under the emperor’s jurisdiction was automatically a Roman, which turns what appears to be an ethnonym into an abstract formality.
One scholar labeled this “a broad, flexible, open-ended concept of ‘Romans’ (in the statist sense),”

in which Roman is defined purely in relation to the state. Stripping Romanness of any specific cultural or ethnic content in this way is another way of denying it. This approach sometimes veers into Orthodox fiction. According to one reading of Byzantine identity, there was no place in Orthodox Byzantium for the distinction between Roman and barbarian.
This replaced the ethnic exclusions that are so prominently on display in the Byzantine sources with modern ecumenism.
zh: 我们现在面临的可能不是罗马人太少，而是罗马人太多的尴尬。一些史学家认为，凡住在帝国之内或皇帝管辖之下的人都自动是罗马人，这把看起来是族名的词变成抽象的形式称谓。
一位学者把这称为“一个宽泛、灵活、开放的‘罗马人’概念（国家意义上）”，
其中罗马纯粹相对于国家来定义。这样剥去罗马性任何具体文化或族群内容，是否认它的另一种方式。这种进路有时滑向正教虚构。按照对拜占庭认同的一种解读，正教拜占庭中根本不会区分罗马人与蛮族。
这种说法用现代普世主义取代了拜占庭史料中明确可见的族群排斥。

en: Yet contrary to these formulas, not everyone living within the empire or serving the emperor was regarded ethnically as a Roman. The Byzantine empire was inhabited by both Romans and non-Romans, and the latter were designated by separate ethnic names and frequently associated with stereotypes. Speros Vryonis has rightly questioned “the often heard generalization that in Byzantium ethnic affiliation was insignificant . . . that the inhabitants of the empire felt that in effect they were all Romans and Christians.” To the contrary, they “were quite aware of ethnic distinctions among the population.”

Moreover, recent attempts to cast the early Byzantine empire as “color-blind” when it came to ethnicity have also elicited legitimate pushback: ethnic differences, for example between Goths and Romans, played a significant role in political conflict.
zh: 然而与这些公式相反，并非所有住在帝国之内或为皇帝服务的人都在族群上被视为罗马人。拜占庭帝国住着罗马人和非罗马人，后者用单独的族名指称，并常与刻板印象挂钩。斯佩罗斯·弗里奥尼斯正确地质疑了“常听到的那种概括，即在拜占庭族群归属无关紧要……帝国居民觉得他们实际上都是罗马人和基督徒”。相反，他们“相当清楚人口中的族群区分”。
此外，近期把早期拜占庭帝国在族群问题上描绘为“色盲”的尝试也引来了正当的反驳：族群差异，例如哥特人与罗马人之间的差异，在政治冲突中起了重要作用。

en: Ethnic others fell into three main groups. First, there were elite men at the court who held offices and commanded armies but who were regarded as ethnic foreigners or had an origin that differentiated them from mainstream Romans, for example the Persarmenian Narses under Justinian; the Armenian Artabasdos under Leon III; the Saracen Samonas under Leon VI; the Norman Rouselios under Michael VII; the Georgian Pakourianos under Alexios I Komnenos; and many more. Mere service was not enough to make one a Roman. However, some officers of foreign origin were more or less Romanized and, if they settled within the empire, their descendants could quickly become indistinguishable from other Romans through processes of assimilation that we will discuss in Chapter 4.
zh: 在族群上被视作外人的人，大致有三类。第一类是宫廷中担任官职、统领军队的精英男性，但他们被视为族群外人，或有使其区别于主流罗马人的出身，例如查士丁尼治下的波斯亚美尼亚人纳尔塞斯；利奥三世治下的亚美尼亚人阿尔塔巴斯多斯；利奥六世治下的萨拉森人萨莫纳斯；米海尔七世治下的诺曼人鲁塞利奥斯；阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁治下的格鲁吉亚人帕库里亚诺斯；还有许多。仅仅为皇帝效力，并不能使人成为罗马人。不过，一些外国出身的军官或多或少罗马化了，如果他们在帝国之内定居，其后裔可以通过我们将在第四章讨论的同化过程迅速变得与其他罗马人无法区分。

en: Evidence for foreigners serving at the imperial court even while they were perceived as “ethnics” or “barbarians” is abundant and comes from all periods. In 542, Justinian released “barbarians who are subject to our polity” and who held the rank of
from the requirement of ratifying their marriages via a contract (i.e., they could use intent alone).

Thus holders of the highest imperial rank could still be seen as barbarians and treated separately from a legal point of view. A manual for organizing court receptions from 899 pays separate attention to “all of the
men who serve the emperor, such as Khazars, Arabs, and Franks . . . who are to enter dressed in their proper ethnic garment, which they call

Dress rules were here enforced to highlight ethnic differences. Interestingly, they were all required to wear a single garment that marked them out as a single class, rather than their respective ethnic apparel. These men may also have occupied an ambiguous legal area. In the collection of legal rulings made by the eleventh-century judge Eustathios Romaios, we find the case of a Georgian

who, despite having a high title at the court, had not followed “the law of the Romans” in drawing up his will. In addition to whatever customs defined this man’s foreignness in Romans eyes, such as his native language, this titular may not even have been operating as a Roman citizen.
