refers to his foreign origin and not his religion, as he was fervently pious. He was called The Barbarian even though he owned a mansion in the City and was important at the court. Dress, law, and names could be used to mark these men out as different.
zh: 各个时期都有大量证据表明，外人为帝国宫廷效力，却仍被视为“异族”或“蛮族”。542年，查士丁尼下令，享有
（illustris）品秩、“臣属于我们政治共同体的蛮族”无须以契约确认婚姻（即仅凭意愿即可缔结婚姻）。
因此，即使享有帝国最高品秩，也仍可能被视为蛮族，在法律上有别于他人。一部899年编成的宫廷觐见手册特别规定，“为皇帝效力的所有
（ethnikoi）男子，如可萨人、阿拉伯人和法兰克人……入内时须穿规定的异族服装，也就是他们所谓的
此处借服饰规章凸显族群差异。有意思的是，所有这些人都得穿同一种衣服来表明他们同属一类，而不是各穿自己群体的服饰。他们的法律地位可能也并不明确。十一世纪法官欧斯塔提奥斯·罗马奥斯的判例汇编记载了一名格鲁吉亚
（ethnikos）的个案：此人虽在宫廷享有高级头衔，却没有按照“罗马人的法律”立遗嘱。在罗马人看来，母语等特征已足以标明他是外人。这位头衔持有者甚至可能没有以罗马公民的身份行事。
《小圣瓦西里传》写的是一位虚构的十世纪圣徒。书中提到一位叫君士坦丁的人，担任
（通常授予宦官的一种宫廷职位），“人人都叫他‘蛮子’，因为他是
这里的
指他的异族出身，与宗教无关。他的信仰十分虔诚。他虽在都城拥有宅邸、在宫廷地位重要，仍被称作“蛮子”。服饰、法律和称呼都可以用来标示这些人的不同。

en: Emperors could appoint both Romans and foreigners to official positions. If Byzantium was a predominantly Roman-ethnic state, we should expect there to have been a degree of prejudice directed against these foreigners at the court, as their success bred resentment among the “native-born.” Indeed, we find such sentiments in the sources.

They were all the product of specific circumstances and should not be taken as the Romans’ default view of the ethnics among them. Chapters 4 and 5 will show how open Byzantium was to foreign settlement and even to groups of immigrants and refugees who were willing to adapt to Roman norms. But the very possibility that the Romans could express such prejudice on ethnic grounds indicates that this was not, at bottom, a nonethnic society but rather a Romanethnic one with minorities. In some cases, emperors made a point of restricting certain positions to Romans.
zh: 皇帝可以任命罗马人和外人担任官职。如果拜占庭是一个以罗马族群为主的国家，那么这些人在宫廷会遭到一定程度的偏见，并不出奇。他们仕途顺遂，使一些“本土出身者”心生怨恨。事实上我们在史料中发现这种情绪。
它们都是特定环境的产物，不应被视为罗马人对其中异族的默认看法。第4、5章将说明拜占庭对外人定居、甚至对愿意适应罗马规范的移民和难民群体多么开放。但罗马人能够基于族群理由表达这种偏见的可能性本身表明，这从根本上不是一个非族群社会，而是一个带少数族群的罗马族群社会。有些情况下，皇帝特意明确规定某些职位只授予罗马人。

en: The second category included ethnic or foreign military units. Roll calls of Byzantine campaign forces in the sources will sometimes list, beside the Romans, various ethnic units such as Huns, Armenians, Pechenegs, Rus’, Varangians, or others.
For example, in 1088 Alexios I Komnenos exempted a monastery from the billeting of soldiers, “including both Roman and

allies, such as Rus’, Varangians, Koulpingoi, Inglinoi [from England], Franks [Normans], Nemitsoi [Germans], Bulgarians, Saracens, Alans, Abasgians, the Immortals, and, in sum, all other Romans and foreigners.”

Such lists refute the notion that whoever served the emperor in a formal sense was considered a Roman, regardless of his ethnicity. Some foreign groups served in the imperial army for long periods but still remained ethnically distinct in the eyes of the Romans. Our sources either give their names or simply call them generically the
(people of another race),
(foreigners), or “barbarians.”
The army could be described collectively as consisting “of men of the same race
along with the foreigners
or “of Romans and soldiers from the
In his laws, Justinian distinguished between “our officers and soldiers and the others, the ethnic types who are allied to our polity.”

Arabic sources often make the same distinctions, for example between “Roman and Armenian” soldiers serving under imperial officers, which proves that they were not imaginary or textual artefacts of elite writing but grounded in contemporary perceptions of ethnic difference.
On the Roman side, these distinctions were not devoid of moral or patriotic valence. For example, Leon VI advised his generals that, if they should have any
of the enemy in their own army (i.e., men of the same race as the enemy), they were to remove them to a different place before the battle through some plausible pretext.
The assumption is that men of the same race might stick together and betray the Romans. On the other hand, Leon admits that foreign spies caught in the Roman camp may be either Romans (suborned) or
(men of foreign birth).
He assumed that his men could tell them apart.
zh: 第二类包括按族群编成的部队或外籍部队。史料中拜占庭出征部队的点名册有时会在罗马人之外列出各种族群单位，如匈人、亚美尼亚人、佩切涅格人、罗斯人、瓦良格人或其他。
例如，1088年阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁免除了一座修道院为士兵提供宿营的义务，“包括罗马士兵和
（ethnikoi）盟军，如罗斯人、瓦良格人、库尔平戈伊人、英格利诺伊人（Inglinoi）［来自英格兰］、法兰克人［诺曼人］、涅米措伊人（Nemitsoi）［德意志人］、保加利亚人、萨拉森人、阿兰人、阿巴斯吉亚人、不死军，总之所有其他罗马人和外人”。
这类清单驳斥了这样一种观念：凡在形式意义上为皇帝服务者，无论族群为何都被视为罗马人。一些外国群体在帝国军队中长期服役，但在罗马人眼中仍保持族群上的独特。我们的史料要么给出他们的名字，要么干脆统称他们为
（allophyloi）、
（ethnikoi）或“蛮族”。
军队可以被整体描述为由“
（homophylon）男子以及
（xenikon）”组成，
或“由罗马人和出身各
（ethne）的士兵”组成。
查士丁尼在其法律中区分“我们的军官和士兵与其他人，即与我们政治共同体结盟的异族”。
阿拉伯史料常作同样区分，例如在帝国军官麾下服役的“罗马与亚美尼亚”士兵之间，这证明它们不是精英文字的想象或文本伪影，而是植根于同时代对族群差异的感知。
在罗马方面，这些区分并非没有道德或爱国意涵。例如，利奥六世告诫他的将军们，如果自己军中有敌人的任何
（homophyloi）（即与敌人同族的人），应在战前通过某个说得过去的借口把他们调往别处。
其假设是同族的人可能抱成一团、背叛罗马人。另一方面，利奥承认在罗马营地抓获的外国间谍可能是罗马人（被收买的）或
（出身异族的人）。
他假定自己的人能分辨他们。

en: These categorical distinctions shaped how the Romans perceived their own armed forces. In his speech addressed to the army in 958— which was probably meant to be read out by criers—Konstantinos VII reminds the soldiers that there are units of barbarians (ἐθνικοί, ἔθνη) fighting alongside them, so the rest should fight bravely to impress the courage of “the Roman
” upon both them and the
(men of the same race, i.e., us Romans).
zh: 这些范畴区分塑造了罗马人看待自己武装力量的方式。在958年向军队发表的演说中——大概是要由传令官宣读的——君士坦丁七世提醒士兵，有蛮族部队（ἐθνικοί, ἔθνη）与他们并肩作战，所以其余人应英勇作战，向他们以及
（homophyloi，即我们罗马人）显示“罗马
（genos）”的勇气。

en: The third and most populous category of non-Romans were ethnic communities that lived in the empire and were subject to imperial institutions. These more than the others broke the equation between being a subject of the emperor and being a Roman. Indeed, it is only because of them that we can call the empire multiethnic to begin with, to whatever degree that term is justified. For example, we saw in Snapshot 1 how the Isaurians were regarded as a non-Roman ethnic group in the fifth century. Unfortunately, we do not know the Isaurian point of view, which was likely not uniform. In middle Byzantium, the Romans perceived other groups as foreign even when they were part of the empire, including the Slavs, Bulgarians, and Armenians. The question at the heart of the question of “empire” is precisely how the Romans governed these non-Roman groups. But before we can study that relationship, we need to know its parties.
zh: 第三类、也是人数最多的非罗马人类别，是住在帝国之内、受帝国制度管辖的族群共同体。这些共同体尤其说明，身为皇帝的臣民，并不等于身为罗马人。事实上，正因为它们，我们才能一开始就称帝国为多族群的，无论这个术语在多大程度上正当。例如，我们在剪影1看到五世纪的伊苏里亚人如何被视为非罗马族群。不幸的是我们不知道伊苏里亚人的观点，那大概并不一致。在中期拜占庭，罗马人把其他群体视为外人，即便它们是帝国的一部分，包括斯拉夫人、保加利亚人和亚美尼亚人。“帝国”问题核心的问题，正是罗马人如何统治这些非罗马群体。但在研究那种关系之前，我们需要知道它的各方。

en: Evidence for the existence of non-Roman ethnic groups within the empire will be presented in Chapters 6 and 7, which will be case studies focusing on the tenth and eleventh centuries. Suffice it to say that the Romans continued to identify these groups by their ethnic names even when they were subjects of the emperor; juxtaposed them to themselves in ways that suggest that they were analogous, nonidentical groups (e.g., Romans and Bulgarians, or Romans and Armenians); identified them as foreign on the basis of birth, culture, language, and religion (where relevant); and spread negative ethnic stereotypes about them.
zh: 帝国内部非罗马族群存在的证据将在第6、7章呈现，那两章是聚焦十、十一世纪的案例研究。只需说，罗马人继续用族名识别这些群体，即便它们是皇帝臣民；将这些群体与自身并提，仿佛它们彼此有别，却可以相提并论（如罗马人与保加利亚人，或罗马人与亚美尼亚人）；根据出身、文化、语言和宗教（在相关处）把它们识别为外人；并传播关于它们的负面族群刻板印象。

en: Here I will note two cases of ethnic prejudice that directly belie the claim that all notional subjects of the emperor were regarded as Romans. In the historian Agathias (sixth century), one of the Roman defendants on trial for the murder of the Laz king Goubazes bursts out with the following inflammatory statement: “Every barbarian race

children: (phylon), even when it is subject to the Romans,

en: is totally different from us in mentality as well as in the order of its laws.”

The speaker was clearly exaggerating for effect. Even other Romans would take this to be an extreme statement coming from a murderer, but it merely sharpens a conventional and widespread perception of difference. In the eleventh century, Eustathios Boïlas wrote in his will that “I became an emigrant from the land which bore me [Cappadocia], and I went a distance of one and one-half weeks from my fatherland. I settled among alien nations with strange religion and tongue.”
He means the Armenians who lived in the empire’s nowexpanded eastern provinces.
zh: 这里我举两个族群偏见的案例，直接反驳所有名义上的皇帝臣民都被视为罗马人的主张。在史学家阿加提阿斯（六世纪）笔下，因谋杀拉兹国王古巴泽斯而受审的罗马被告之一迸出以下煽动性陈述：“每个蛮族
（phylon），
，在心态和法律秩序上都与我们完全不同。”
说话者显然为了增强效果而夸大其词。连其他罗马人也会认为这是出自一个谋杀者的极端陈述，但它只是强化了一种常规而广泛的差异感知。十一世纪，欧斯塔提奥斯·博伊拉斯在遗嘱中写道：“我成了离开生我之地［卡帕多西亚］的移民，走到离我祖国一周半路程的地方。我定居在宗教与语言陌生的异族中间。”
他指的是住在帝国扩张后的东部行省的亚美尼亚人。

en: Conversely, there were circumstances in which assuming an ethnicity might have been advantageous, even if the claim was false, for example in order to register in a military unit for Goths that enjoyed various privileges.
Psellos claimed that magicians and charlatans had no real skill but gave out as credentials their “ethnic origins, the one claiming to be an Illyrian, the other a Persian.”
zh: 反过来，某些情况下，声称自己属于某个族群可能有利可图，即便主张是假的，例如为了登记进一个享有各种特权的哥特人军事单位。
普塞洛斯声称，魔法师和江湖骗子没有真本事，却拿“族群出身”当资质，一个自称伊利里亚人，另一个自称波斯人。

en: If the formal criterion of being subject to the emperor does not identify anyone as a Roman, we must look for different criteria. Conversely, Romans could retain their ethnicity even outside the empire, when they were in barbarian captivity, at least for a few generations. This reinforces the point that imperial jurisdiction and Romanness did not always overlap. In Snapshot 2, we discussed the story in the

of the provincial Romans who were enslaved by Avars yet managed to preserve their identity in foreign captivity and through intermarriage, until their descendants yearned to return home. Consider also a story that is told about Michael I (811–813). That emperor was approached by two groups of refugees who wanted to settle in the empire, one a group of Bulgars “who picked up, departed from their ancestral dwellings, and came to the land of the Romans,” while the other were “some of the Romans who had been taken captive [by the Bulgars] in the previous war, had escaped their captivity, and had now come back to their homelands.”
Their identity was obviously not a function of the title claimed by their ruler at any time. They were Romans who desired to return to the Roman homeland.
zh: 如果仅凭是否臣属于皇帝不能判定一个人是否罗马人，我们必须寻找不同标准。反过来，罗马人即便在帝国之外沦为蛮族俘虏，也能维持族群认同，至少几代人。这强化了帝国管辖权与罗马性并不总重叠的论点。剪影2中我们讨论了《圣德米特里奥斯圣迹集》里行省罗马人被阿瓦尔人奴役、却在外族手中沦为俘虏、与外族通婚的情况下仍设法保存认同、直到后裔渴望归乡的故事。再看看一个关于米海尔一世（811–813年在位）的故事。两群想在帝国定居的难民接近那位皇帝，一群是保加尔人，“他们收拾行装，离开祖居，来到罗马人的土地”，另一群是“一些罗马人，他们在前次战争中被［保加尔人］掳走，逃出了俘虏生涯，如今回到故土”。
显然，他们的认同并不取决于统治者在不同时期声称拥有何种头衔。他们是渴望回到罗马故土的罗马人。

en: A Prima Facie Ethnicity
zh: 族群存在的初步证据

en: Let us triangulate our results so far and see what kind of group these Romans formed. The Roman community apparently included most provincials regardless of gender, class, or occupation, except for those who are noted as belonging to specific ethnic groups, such as Slavs, Bulgarians, and Armenians. Language, religion, and other cultural attributes such as dress were occasionally used to mark, justify, and police these differences. The Romans could also be imagined as a community of descent and kinship, though they could at times absorb and assimilate members of other groups. When cut off from their homeland, they could sustain their group identity for at least a few generations.
zh: 让我们把迄今所得放在一起，互相参照，看看这些罗马人构成哪种群体。罗马共同体显然包括大多数行省人，无论性别、阶级或职业，除了那些被注明属于特定族群者，如斯拉夫人、保加利亚人和亚美尼亚人。语言、宗教和服饰等其他文化属性偶尔被用来标示这些差异、给出划分理由并维护族群界线。罗马人也可以被想象为一个世系与亲属共同体，尽管他们有时能吸收同化其他群体的成员。与故土隔绝时，他们能维持群体认同至少几代人。

en: There is only one type of group that fits this contour: it is an ethnic group (or a nation, depending on the definition). It is important to be explicit about the force and limitations of this conclusion. It is a prima facie model that accounts for the overall shape of the Roman community that is reflected in the sources; for the patterns of inclusion and exclusion that demarcated it from other groups of the same analytical order; and for some of the ways in which its members talked about their in-group. We have also encountered some of the specific criteria of inclusion and exclusion, that is, the contents of the identity in question, and these too strongly suggest that we are dealing with an ethnicity. In much scholarship on ancient and medieval ethnicities, especially the extinct ones, this mere outline is often sufficient to establish the historical existence of such a group, at least on a presumptive basis. In our case, the surviving record is large enough that, in Chapter 3, we can go further and discuss the individual ethnic indicia in more detail.
zh: 只有一种群体符合这个轮廓：它是一个族群（或一个民族，取决于定义）。重要的是明确这个结论的力度与局限。它是一个初步模型，解释了史料反映的罗马共同体总体形状；解释了把它与属于同一分析范畴的其他群体区别开来的纳入与排除模式；也解释了其成员谈论自己所属群体的一些方式。我们还遇到了纳入与排除的一些具体标准，即所讨论认同的内容，这些也强烈暗示这里所讨论的是一个族群。研究古代和中世纪群体、特别是已不复存在的族群时，仅凭这个轮廓往往就足以确立这样一个群体的历史存在，至少作初步推定。在我们的案例中，存世材料足够丰富，因此在第3章我们可以更进一步，更详细地讨论各个族群标记。

en: If the Romans of Byzantium thought of themselves as a group that fits modern definitions of ethnicity—and it seems that they did—that suffices for present purposes. In addition to the evidence for this conclusion, we have the fact that they sometimes called themselves an
or a
a word that, whether literally or metaphorically, stressed the kinship of their community. However, the way in which they used these two words bears further comment.
zh: 如果拜占庭的罗马人把自己看作一个符合现代族群性定义的群体——看来确实如此——那就足以满足当前目的。除了支持这一结论的证据，我们还有这样一个事实：他们有时自称
或
，后一个词无论取字面义还是比喻义，都强调共同体的亲缘关系。然而他们使用这两个词的方式值得进一步评论。

en: The eastern Romans had a dual way of talking about
that may cause confusion. In one sense—according to one modality of discourse—they followed the ancient ethnographic tradition in using the term

for any group that was constituted by a more or less specific cluster of what we would call ethnic traits, such as a distinctive language, religion, political organization, ethnonym, social mores, possibly shared descent, and the like. In this conception, the Romans of Byzantium were only one such group among many others. But there was a different sense in which the Romans stood on one side of a divide and all the foreign “nations”
collectively stood on the other. This usage had two roots that came together in Byzantium. The first was the ancient convention of dividing the world between Romans and conquered
The second was an Old Testament model that divided the world between the Chosen People and the “gentiles” or “nations,” which in Greek was translated as “the
” or the
(plural).
Here the Byzantines, as Christian Romans, were a new Chosen People surrounded by hostile
who were typically regarded as savage, heathen, and inferior.
zh: 东部罗马人有两种使用
的方式，可能引起混淆。在一种意义上——按一种话语模式——他们遵循古代民族志传统，用
指由一系列多少可以辨认的族群特征构成的群体，如独特语言、宗教、政治组织、族名、社会风俗、可能的共同世系等等。在这个观念中，拜占庭的罗马人只是众多此类群体中的一个。但还有另一种意义，罗马人站在分界线的一侧，所有外国“民族”（
）集体站在另一侧。这种用法有两个在拜占庭汇合的根源。第一个是把世界划分为罗马人与被征服的
的古代惯例。
第二个是《旧约》模型，把世界划分为选民与“外邦人”或“万民”，希腊语译为
或
（复数）。
这里拜占庭人作为基督徒罗马人，是一个被敌对的
包围的新选民，那些
通常被视为野蛮、异教、低劣。

en: For example, in the exchange between Louis II and Basileios I that we discussed in Chapter 1, Basileios seems to have argued in his original (lost) letter that Louis could not be the emperor of the Romans because he came from a
one of the nations. Apparently, this implied that the Romans were a people who stood apart from the rest. In surviving texts that reflect this division, the Romans call themselves not an
but a
or a
(a people).
There were weaker and stronger versions of this model. The stronger might imply a full theory of the Byzantines as a new Chosen People on biblical lines, while in the weaker the
were just barbarians who surrounded the Roman empire and who might even be Christians themselves.
Either way, the Romans never ceased to perceive the world as fundamentally divided between “the nations” and “our own people,” or “the nations” and “the
of the Romans.”
zh: 例如，在我们第1章讨论的路易二世与瓦西里一世的交锋中，瓦西里似乎在其原信（已佚）中论证，路易不能做罗马人的皇帝，因为他出自一个
，即诸民族之一。显然这暗示罗马人是站在其余之外的一个人民。在反映这种划分的存世文本中，罗马人不自称
，而称
或
（人民）。
这个模型有较弱和较强版本。较强版本可能暗示一套按圣经路线把拜占庭人视为新选民的完整理论，而较弱版本中
只是环绕罗马帝国的蛮族，他们自己甚至可能是基督徒。
无论如何，罗马人从未停止把世界感知为根本划分为“诸民族”与“我们自己的人民”，或“诸民族”与“罗马人的

en: We therefore have two models: according to the first, the world is full of ethnic groups or nations and the Romans are one among them, even if a superior one, while according to the second the incomparable
or
of the Romans (or Christians) is surrounded by a sea of hostile

Needless to say, the second view is more amenable to the sacralization of Byzantine identity and its elevation from the mundane world of nations and ethnic groups into a more transcendent realm of theological abstraction, a move that many scholars prefer. Compared to the paratactic equivalence of the old ethnographic model, the ancient imperialist-biblical model took a more exclusive stance, which may have verged on treating the in-group as exceptional: ethnic traits mattered for foreigners only, while the Christian Romans provided the nonethnic norm against which the others were measured.
This is like whites today who believe that ethnicity and ethnic studies apply to minorities, to brown or black people, not to what they implicitly take to be the “norm,” that is, their own whiteness.
zh: 因此我们有两个模型：按第一个，世界充满族群或民族，罗马人是其中之一，哪怕是优越的一个；按第二个，无可比拟的罗马人（或基督徒）
或
被敌对的
的汪洋包围。不用说，第二个看法更便于把拜占庭认同神圣化，把它从民族与族群的世俗世界抬升到更具超越性的抽象神学领域，许多学者更愿这样做。与旧民族志模型的并列对等相比，古代帝国主义—圣经模型采取更排他的立场，可能近乎把内群体当作例外：族群特征只对外人重要，而基督徒罗马人提供了衡量他者的非族群规范。
这就像今天有些白人相信族群性和族群研究适用于少数群体、棕肤色或黑肤色的人，而不适用于他们隐含视为“规范”的东西，即他们自己的白人性。

en: The two models, however, are not incompatible. They were merely two different ways of talking about ethnic difference, the one paratactic and the other hierarchical. Calling the Romans “a people of God” who were distinct from “the nations” is perfectly compatible with the Romans also being an ethnic group. It means only that they viewed themselves as unique and superior to all others. As mentioned above, this model preferred the word
for the superior group. But in ancient and Christian texts,
too could refer to peoples, ethnic groups, and nations.
even
ethnicity as its etymology stresses kinship bonds over other aspects of group cohesion, so the national
is effectively an extended family.
zh: 然而两个模型并不互斥。它们只是谈论族群差异的两种不同方式，一种把各群体并列，另一种按高下区分。称罗马人为区别于“诸民族”的“上帝子民”，与罗马人同时也是一个族群完全相容。它只意味着他们自视独特、优于所有他者。如上所述，后一种话语通常用
指称地位优越的群体。但在古代和基督教文本中，
也可以指人民、族群和民族。
甚至能
族群性，因为在词源上，它较群体的其他凝聚因素更强调亲缘纽带。因此，作为一个民族的
实际上就是一个大家族。

en: Moreover, the argument for a Roman ethnicity is not based primarily on lexicography but on the presence and awareness of ethnic indicia, and the latter could just as well be marshaled under the term
as the term

Besides, the biblical image of the Jewish people surrounded by many hostile “nations” has functioned throughout Christian history as an archetype for the formation of exclusive ethnic or national identities and as a model for medieval and modern nations.
In fact, it was possible even within the biblical paradigm to refer to Christian Romans as an
so long as one added the adjective “holy,” which apparently canceled the negative associations of the biblical word
zh: 此外，罗马族群性的论证主要不是基于词汇学，而是基于实际存在的种种族群标志，以及人们对它们的认识。这些标志既可以归入
，也可以归入
。再说，犹太人民被众多敌对“民族”包围的圣经意象，在整个基督教历史中一直充当排他性族群或民族认同形成的原型，以及中世纪和现代民族的模型。
事实上，即便在圣经范式内，也可以用
来称呼信奉基督教的罗马人，只要冠以“神圣”一词，这显然能消除圣经用语
的负面联想。

en: Outside this biblical paradigm,

was a banal term in Byzantium, as it just meant a foreigner, a non-Roman; it was not always linked to theological views of history. I will cite two instances. The name of the frontiersman Digenis (“Of Dual Descent”) is explained by the poet by the fact that he was an
on his father’s side and a Roman on his mother’s.

This poem is as close to the vernacular and even folk level that we can get for this period (ca. 1100) and it proves beyond a doubt that being a Roman was, at least in part, understood to be a matter of descent. In a normal field of studies, this passage alone would suffice to establish ethnicity as a base sense for how many Byzantines saw themselves to be Romans (even a single specimen of life on Mars suffices for a big conclusion). The second example occurs in a thirteenth-century chronicle, where the author lists all the categories of people an emperor wanted to benefit. Each pair, in its complementarity, is meant to convey the sense of
“Urban and rural, slave and free, noble and common,
and Roman, poor and rich, worthy and unworthy, and every person of whatever station in life.”
The pairing of Roman and
as an exclusive complementary pair means that “Roman” encompassed both rural and urban Romans, rich and poor Romans, and so on.
zh: 在这个圣经范式之外，
在拜占庭是个常见词，只指外人，也就是非罗马人；并不总与神学历史观挂钩。我举两个例子。边疆英雄迪格尼斯名字的意思是“双重世系”。按诗人的解释，他父系是
（ethnikos），母系则是罗马人。
这首诗是我们对这个时期（约1100年）所能得到的最接近口语乃至民间层面的文本，它毫无疑问地证明，做罗马人至少部分被理解为世系问题。在一个正常研究领域，仅这一段就足以确立族群性是许多拜占庭人理解自己做罗马人的基础含义（哪怕一个火星生命标本也足以得出大结论）。第二个例子出现在一部十三世纪编年史中，作者列出一位皇帝想惠及的所有人类别。每两个类别互补，都是为了表达“
”：“城里人和乡下人，奴隶和自由人，贵族和平民，异族（
）和罗马人，穷人和富人，当得此惠和不当得此惠的人，以及地位无论如何的每一个人。”
“罗马人”和“异族”这两个类别既相互排斥，又彼此互补，这，意味着“罗马”涵盖乡村与城市罗马人、富与穷罗马人，等等。

en: I have been told by many colleagues that the Byzantine Romans could not have been an ethnic group because they never called themselves an
only a
I have encountered this claim in print only once in recent reading,
but it seems to be widespread, a kind of urban legend that circulates in the field. It is conceptually flawed in two ways: first, because

could also potentially refer to an ethnic group and, second, because the conclusion that the Romans were an ethnic group does not depend on whether they used this word or that, but on whether they distinguished Romans from nonRomans on the basis of what we would identify as ethnic traits. Moreover, the claim is factually wrong, as we have already seen. While
usually referred to foreigners, the Romans are called an

and treated as one among many ethnic groups in a wide variety of texts, including histories, horoscopes, religious disputations, and military manuals. We saw the emperor Konstantinos VII call his Romans an
on the grounds of language, kinship, and the full taxonomy of ethnographic indicia that he was willing to apply to foreign people too.
Both Romans and others, then, were frequently understood to be categories of the same order.
zh: 许多同事告诉我，拜占庭罗马人不可能是一个族群，因为他们从不自称
，只称
。我最近阅读中只在印刷品里遇到过一次这个主张，
但它似乎流传甚广，是本学科流传的一种都市传说。它在概念上有两个缺陷：第一，
也可能指一个族群；第二，罗马人是一个族群的结论不取决于他们用这个词还是那个词，而取决于他们是否基于我们会认定为族群特征的东西区分罗马人与非罗马人。此外，这个主张在事实上是错的，我们已经看到。虽然
通常指外人，罗马人在多种文本里却被称为
、并被当作众多族群之一对待，包括史书、星占、宗教辩论和军事手册。我们看到君士坦丁七世皇帝依据语言、亲缘关系等一整套民族志标准，将罗马人称为一个
，也按同一标准来界定外族。
于是罗马人和他者都经常被理解为同一层次的群体。

en: Of interest here are the lists of nations or ethnic groups produced by some authors, in which Romans are listed paratactically among others. Referring to the missions of the Apostles, John Chrysostom listed Scythians, Thracians, Romans, Persians, Moors, Indians, and Egyptians.

He may have been thinking here of the Romans of ancient Rome rather than of his own contemporaries, but in the end it makes no difference: what matters is the type of category that the word signified in his usage and that of his contemporaries (and, besides, the relevant Romans in the New Testament were those addressed by Paul in Greek and not in Latin, so they were more like Byzantines). The sixth-century author known as Kosmas Indikopleustes, who championed the divine supremacy of the Roman empire, refers in a similar context to Bactrians, Huns, Persians, Indians, Bulgars, Goths, Romans, Franks, and others.
Similar lists, updated for the times, were produced down to the fifteenth century, and the Romans feature in them as one among many Christian
zh: 这里有意思的是某些作者制作的民族或族群清单，其中罗马人与其他并列。谈到使徒的传教活动时，金口约翰列出斯基泰人、色雷斯人、罗马人、波斯人、摩尔人、印度人和埃及人。
他这里想的可能不是同时代人而是古罗马的罗马人，但归根结底没有区别：重要的是这个词在他及其同时代人用法中所指的范畴类型（再说，《新约》中相关的罗马人是保罗用希腊语而非拉丁语致信的对象，所以他们更像拜占庭人）。六世纪作者、被称为科斯马斯·印第科普勒斯特斯的人拥护罗马帝国的神圣至上，他在类似语境中提到巴克特里亚人、匈人、波斯人、印度人、保加尔人、哥特人、罗马人、法兰克人等等。
类似清单随时代更新，一直制作到十五世纪，罗马人在其中是众多基督教
之一。

en: Moreover, the Romans of Byzantium did often imagine themselves as an extended kinship group. This was the basis for Manuel’s objection to the proposal made by his father Andronikos I Komnenos to execute all his enemies and their entire families: such a plan would eventually kill “all the Romans” (Snapshot 4). We hear of people who were “Roman by birth.” For example, in the lay
a girl says that she fell in love with a man of Roman birth, and Digenis is said to be Roman on his mother’s side only.
We hear of people who were Romans by birth but had been raised among foreigners, where they had become culturally foreign.

If being Roman was a function only of cultural profile, then these kinds of statements would not be possible; so too if being Roman meant only that one was a subject of the empire. Birth and descent counted. Conversely, we hear of men who were foreigners by birth (e.g., Italians, Turks, or Tzanoi) but who were raised as Romans and effectively treated as such.
Birth
a factor, though it could be overcome by acculturation, a dynamic to which the sources were sensitive, as we will see throughout.
zh: 此外，拜占庭的罗马人确实经常把自己想象为一个范围广泛的亲缘群体。这是曼努埃尔反对其父安德罗尼库斯一世·科穆宁处死所有敌人及其全家提议的基础：这样一个计划最终会杀死“所有罗马人”（剪影4）。我们听说有人“生来是罗马人”。例如，在叙事诗《迪格尼斯》中，一个女孩说她爱上了一个罗马出身的男人，而迪格尼斯据说只在母系是罗马人。
我们听说有人生来是罗马人，却在外人中长大，在文化上逐渐变得和外族人一样。
如果罗马人身份完全取决于文化特征，这类陈述就不可能；如果做罗马人只意味着做帝国臣民，也一样。出身和血缘确实有关。反过来，我们听说有人生来是外人（如意大利人、突厥人或扎诺伊人），却被养育成罗马人、实际上被当作罗马人对待。
出身
是一个因素，不过文化适应也能改变由出身带来的认同。这一过程在史料中也有所体现，下文还会不断见到。

en: It was also possible, in some contexts, to imagine the Romans as a large family. The national Roman collective could rhetorically take the place of one’s birth family, a sure sign that we are in the presence of a national ideology. For example, an orator of the late thirteenth century, Maximos Planoudes, decided to talk about the Roman
as a whole when he came to the part in his speech reserved for an emperor’s parents and ancestors. The nation appears here as the king’s proper family.
In 867, the patriarch Photios self-consciously reached back to classical antiquity in order to bestow upon Michael III the title “father of the fatherland”
adding that he surpassed Cyrus and Augustus in that role.
In his verse epitaph, Basileios II (976–1025) boasted that throughout his long life he had “guarded the children of New Rome” by marching along the frontiers.

These were the paternalistic aspects of a ruling ideology that saw the Roman community as an extended family. The language of kinship could, then, be applied generally to the relationship that bound Romans together, including the relationship between all Romans and their state.
zh: 有些语境中还可以把罗马人想象为一个大家庭。整个罗马民族在修辞上可以取代一个人出身的家庭，这是我们面对一种民族意识形态的明确标志。例如，十三世纪后期一位演说家马克西莫斯·普拉努德斯，在演说中留给皇帝父母与祖先的部分，选择谈论整个罗马
（genos）。民族在这里作为国王的真正家庭出现。
867年，牧首佛提乌有意回溯古典古代，授予米海尔三世“祖国之父”（pater patriae）头衔，并补充说他在那个角色上超过居鲁士和奥古斯都。
瓦西里二世（976–1025年在位）在其诗体墓志铭中夸耀，漫长一生中他通过沿边境行军“守护了新罗马的孩子们”。
这些用语体现了统治意识形态家长式的一面，即视罗马共同体为一个大家庭。于是亲属语言可以普遍应用于把罗马人绑在一起的关系，包括所有罗马人与其国家之间的关系。

en: This explains the intuitive logic displayed in texts according to which Romans should side with Romans and not with foreigners, and that preference should be given to people of one’s own
or
(add the prefix
-) and not to those who were “other” (add the prefix
-). More texts than can be surveyed here urge such an ethic of national solidarity, a reminder that the Romans needed given their propensity for civil war.

I highlight two military manuals to show how state policy and hortatory rhetoric built on and tried to evoke Roman ethnic solidarity. The military author Syrianos (ninth century) says that defensive war brings salvation to “the people of our own race”
We must fight back, he says, for our enemies attack our religious faith and fatherland
and we have to fight “on account of the love that we have for each other. . . . We have to do what is just, for we are Romans and we should imitate the virtue of our ancestors [the ancient Romans].”
Syrianos sometimes addresses his audience directly as “Roman men.”
Defensive war by the state was therefore not only justified but required in order to protect people of the same race, an extended family. This effectively cast the empire as a large “fatherland”
or homeland of the Roman people.
zh: 这解释了文本中展示的直觉逻辑：罗马人应站在罗马人一边而非外人一边，应优先考虑
（genos）、
（ethnos）或
（phylon）相同的人（加前缀
-，即“同”），而非“他者”（加前缀
-，即“异”）。还有许多无法在此逐一讨论的文本，也倡导这种民族团结的伦理。考虑到罗马人动辄内战，他们的确需要这样的提醒。
我突出两部军事手册，展示国家政策与劝勉修辞如何建立在罗马族群团结之上并试图唤起它。军事论著作者叙里亚诺斯（九世纪）说，防御战给“我们同族的人”（homophyloi）带来拯救。他说我们必须反击，因为敌人攻击我们的宗教信仰和祖国（patris），我们必须“因我们彼此之间的爱而战……我们必须行正义，因为我们是罗马人，应效仿我们祖先［古罗马人］的美德”。
叙里亚诺斯有时直接称听众为“罗马男人们”。
因此国家的防御战不仅正当而且必需，以保护同族的人——一个扩展家庭。这实际上把帝国塑造为一个大的“祖国”（patris），即罗马人民的故土。

en: These were not expressions of an exclusive military fraternity. The imagined “family” here was the Roman nation as a whole, not just the army corps. In his military manual (ca. 900), Leon VI echoed the sentiments of Syrianos and wrote to his generals that when the enemy ravages “our land . . . it is right to take up war on behalf of our subjects . . . your brothers.”

As the empire was surrounded by non-Christian enemies between the sixth and the ninth centuries, appeals to Roman patriotism and Christian solidarity effectively overlapped. For Leon, devotion to Rome and to Christ went hand in hand (he had not yet fully processed the conversion of Bulgaria, which threw a wrench into this equation for him). He too uses kinship language in talking about fighting on behalf of the homeland and the faith. For example, heralds should instruct the army that “the war is on behalf of God, and the love that we have for him, and for the entire

It is, moreover, on behalf of our brothers in the faith and, if this applies, for our women, children, and fatherland. They should say that the memory of those who excel in war on behalf of our brothers’ freedom will be eternal.”
zh: 这些话并非只是在表达军人内部的兄弟情谊。这里想象的“家庭”是整个罗马民族，不只是军团。在其军事手册（约900年）中，利奥六世呼应叙里亚诺斯的情感，写信给将军们说，当敌人蹂躏“我们的土地……正当的做法是为我们的臣民……你们的兄弟而战”。
由于六至九世纪帝国被非基督徒敌人包围，对罗马爱国主义和基督教团结的呼吁实际上重叠。对利奥来说，忠于罗马与忠于基督携手并进（他还没有完全想清保加利亚改宗意味着什么，这给他原有的两相对应带来了麻烦）。他在谈论为故土和信仰而战时也使用亲属语言。例如，传令官应告诉军队：“战争是为上帝、为我们对他的爱、也为整个
（ethnos）。此外，它是为我们信仰中的兄弟，在适用的情况下，也为我们的妇女、儿童和祖国。他们应说，那些为兄弟的自由而英勇作战的人，将永远被人铭记。”

en: How much weight should we give to these expressions of Roman kinship and how did they operate? There are two ways in which a nation of this size may imagine itself as a kinship group. The one is horizontal, in real time: Romans today are born from other Romans. As we saw, the Byzantines certainly had the notion that one could be born a Roman, Ῥωμαῖος τὸ γένος, as opposed to, say, a Turk, Τοῦρκος τὸ γένος. The other way is vertical, reaching back to the distant past: according to this schema, Romans are collectively descended from the ancient Romans. Did the Byzantine Romans believe that they were collectively descended from the ancient Romans too?
zh: 这些关于罗马人彼此有亲缘关系的说法有多大分量？这样的说法又如何起作用？这样一个规模的民族，可以用两种方式把自己想象成亲缘群体。一种是横向的，指当世罗马人出自其他罗马人。如前所述，拜占庭人确有生来就是罗马人的观念，称为 Ῥωμαῖος τὸ γένος（按出身是罗马人），与例如 Τοῦρκος τὸ γένος（按出身是突厥人）相对。另一种是纵向的，可以上溯至遥远的过去。照这种说法，罗马人作为一个群体，是古罗马人的后裔。拜占庭的罗马人是否同样相信，他们作为一个群体是古罗马人的后裔？

en: This is harder to document. It probably formed only a vague aspect of Romanness in Byzantium; I doubt many people thought about it in explicit terms. But it was presupposed in many discursive practices. Merely by calling themselves Romans they asserted a continuity between themselves and the ancient Romans, whose default, unreflexive mode in traditional societies was genetic. In many contexts, the Byzantines called these putative ancestors “the ancient (πάλαι) Romans,” to distinguish them from the Romans of their day, that is, themselves, but also to underscore their continuity. The historian Attaleiates, for example, wrote a long comparison between ancient and modern Romans to prove that the latter, his own people, failed to live up to the standards of glory set by their ancestors.

Such comparisons were not limited to the authors of classicizing histories. The ninth-century monk Euodios wrote the martyrdom of the forty-two military martyrs of Amorion, who were killed after the Muslims took that city in 838. He saw his world as divided between the Romans and the Ishmaelites, and he has the saints at one point speak and refer “to the Romans of old, who conquered the entire world.”

They were making the point to their Muslim captors that one did not need to have the one true faith in order to win a war. Likewise, the provincial author, a monk, of the life of the southern Italian saint Elias the Younger (tenth century) has his hero admonish an imperial general to restrain his men, and in order to persuade him he cites the example of virtuous ancient generals, including Scipio, “who was also a Roman general,”
that is,
zh: 用材料证明这一点更难。它大概只构成拜占庭罗马性的一个模糊面向；我怀疑许多人明确想过它。但它在许多话语实践中被预设。仅仅自称罗马人，他们就断言了自己与古罗马人之间的连续性，而传统社会往往想当然地用血缘世系理解这种延续。在许多语境中，拜占庭人称这些假定祖先为“古代（πάλαι）罗马人”，以区别于他们那个时代的罗马人，即他们自己，但也强调他们的连续性。例如史学家阿塔雷阿特斯写了一段古今罗马人的长篇比较，证明后者——他自己的人民——未能达到祖先设定的荣耀标准。
这类比较不限于古典化史书的作者。九世纪修士欧奥迪奥斯写了阿莫里翁四十二位军人殉道者的殉道记，他们在838年穆斯林攻占该城后被杀。他把他的世界看作划分为罗马人与以实玛利人，并让圣徒们在一处说话时提到“古时的罗马人，他们征服了整个世界”。
他们向俘获他们的穆斯林说明这一点：不需要拥有唯一真信仰也能打赢战争。同样，南意大利《小圣埃利亚斯传》（十世纪）也出自行省的一位修士。他笔下的圣徒劝诫一位帝国将军约束部下，为说服他而引用有德古代将军的例子，包括西庇阿，“他也是罗马将军”，

en: Political continuity could also be taken to imply biological continuity. Consider Justinian’s comment on the title “satrap” used in one of his four Armenian provinces: this, he says, “was not a Roman name, and was unknown to our ancestors, but was introduced from some foreign polity.”

Moreover, Byzantine chronicles trace the history of the Roman polity from antiquity to the Byzantine present without break or ethnic rupture. The symbolic “bridge” between the two was the career of Constantine the Great, who built New Rome and, according to the Byzantine imagination, populated it with nobles whom he brought from Elder Rome.

This may have been enough to establish a sufficient or symbolic link of biological continuity between the two Romes. Also, as we will see in Chapter 3, Byzantine writers called Latin their “ancestral language,” which implies that they viewed the ancient Romans as their own ancestors. By contrast, when they talked about the ancient Greeks, whether in works of elite literature or just in church, they referred to them in a distant way, as a people of the ancient world who were no longer around in the present, the way we might talk about ancient Egyptians or Phrygians.
zh: 政治连续性也可以被理解为暗示生物连续性。想想查士丁尼对其四个亚美尼亚行省之一所用“总督”（satrap）头衔的评论：他说这“不是罗马名字，我们的祖先不知道，而是从某个外国政治共同体引入的”。
此外，拜占庭编年史把罗马政治共同体的历史从古代追溯到拜占庭当下，没有中断，也没有族群上的断裂。两者之间的象征“桥梁”是君士坦丁大帝的事业，他建造新罗马，并按拜占庭人的想象，他从旧罗马带来了贵族，让他们在新城定居。
这也许足以在两座罗马城之间建立血缘连续性的关联，即使这种关联仅具象征性。此外，正如第三章将看到的，拜占庭作者称拉丁语为他们的“祖先语言”，这暗示他们把古罗马人视为自己的祖先。相比之下，当他们谈论古希腊人时，无论在精英著作中还是只在教会里，都以疏远的方式指称他们，作为一个古代世界的人民、如今已不在场，就像我们谈论古埃及人或弗里吉亚人那样。

en: In some contexts, biological continuity from ancient Rome was asserted more explicitly, for example in the army. In a speech to his army, the emperor Julian in 363 referred to the conquerors of Carthage and Spain—over five hundred years before—as “our forefathers.”

In 589, the bishop of Antioch, Gregorios, restored order to an army that had mutinied by addressing the soldiers as “Roman men” and challenging them to prove that they were true Romans and not the “illegitimate children” of their ancestors, who included Romans of the Republic such as Manlius Torquatus.

A church liturgy for fallen soldiers, dating probably from the tenth century and produced in the provinces, refers to the sanctified heroes as the “offspring of Rome,” calling them also the foundation of the
and the entire

During the passage of the Second Crusade in 1147, the emperor Manuel I Komnenos warned the German king Conrad not to pick a fight with the Romans, that is, his own people, whose ancient “ancestors” had conquered a large part of the globe, including the Germans of that time.
In military contexts, therefore, when the Byzantine sources mention “ancestors” they often mean the glorious Romans of old.
zh: 有些语境中，从古罗马的生物连续性被更明确地断言，例如在军队中。363年，尤利安皇帝在向军队的演说中把五百多年前迦太基和西班牙的征服者称为“我们的先祖”。
589年，安条克主教格里高利通过称士兵为“罗马男人们”、挑战他们证明自己是真罗马人而非祖先的“私生子”，恢复了一支哗变军队的秩序，那些祖先包括共和国的罗马人如曼利乌斯·托尔夸图斯。
一篇为阵亡士兵而作的教会礼文，大约于十世纪写于行省。它称那些被尊为神圣的英雄为“罗马的后裔”，并称他们为
（patris）和整个

1147年第二次十字军东征经过时，曼努埃尔一世·科穆宁皇帝警告德意志国王康拉德不要与罗马人——即他自己的人民——挑事，其古代“祖先”曾征服地球很大一部分，包括当时的日耳曼人。
因此在军事语境中，拜占庭史料提到“祖先”时，往往指古时荣耀的罗马人。

en: This link functioned rhetorically, but we should not dismiss it for that reason. Rhetorical appeals are emotive and must correspond to something. And ancient Roman ancestry was invoked in other contexts as well. When emperors and elite Byzantines concocted fake genealogies, they tended to claim ancient Roman ancestry, though by no means exclusively. We saw in Snapshot 1 how Anastasios I claimed descent from Pompey the Great, and similar claims can be traced down to the Palaiologan period.

This was part of Byzantium’s “Roman impulse,” and it could justify actions in nonmilitary spheres too. For example, a hostile source reports that the emperor Theophilos (829–842) was going bald and therefore decreed that “no Roman” should wear hair longer than below the neck; for this, he invoked the practice of “the Roman ancestors, who wore their hair in this way.”

This was rather antiquarian, but the story—or the emperor’s policy, if we accept it as historical, or the author’s joke, if that’s all it was—presupposes an ethnic notion of what it meant to be Roman and a normative standard derived from ancient Rome. None of it would make sense if the Byzantine Romans did not believe that they were in some way descended from the ancient Romans.
zh: 这种联系在修辞层面发挥作用，但我们不应因此就轻视它。修辞诉求带有情感色彩，且必有所指。古罗马祖先在其他语境中也被援引。当皇帝与拜占庭精英编造虚假谱系时，他们往往声称他们是古罗马人的后裔，不过绝非个个如此。我们在剪影1中已看到阿纳斯塔修斯一世如何自称庞培大帝的后裔，类似的声称一直可追溯到巴列奥略时期。
这是拜占庭“罗马冲动”的一部分，它也能为非军事领域的行动提供正当性。例如，一则敌对史料记载，皇帝狄奥斐卢斯（829–842年在位）日渐秃顶，便下令“任何罗马人”的头发都不得长过颈部；为此他援引了“以这种方式留发的罗马祖先”的做法。
这颇有些好古癖的味道，但这个故事——或者皇帝的政策（若我们承认它是史实），或者作者的玩笑（若它仅此而已）——预设了一种关于何为罗马人的族群观念，以及一套源自古罗马的规范标准。如果拜占庭的罗马人不相信自己在某种程度上是古罗马人的后裔，这一切都将毫无意义。

en: The fiction of kinship and descent from the ancient Romans was only one side of the picture, however. As we will see when we turn to assimilation in the second part of this book, Byzantium was also capable of absorbing groups and individuals whose ancestry was partly or even wholly foreign and treating them as fully Roman, so long as they adopted and exhibited the requisite cultural traits; that is, so long as they
Roman through acculturation. Such people might appear in the sources as “a Turk by
but raised as a Roman.”

en: This had a long history in Roman tradition. More than any other ancient polity, Rome incorporated foreign peoples and admitted them to its citizenship and name, even though some Romans did talk about blood purity. That claim is not extensively documented, but it was made.

The dominant logic, however, was of assimilation. A community formed through social consensus, and that moreover knew itself to be so formed, could nevertheless still cast itself as a community of descent. As has been written about ancient Rome:
zh: 这在罗马传统中有着悠久的历史。罗马比任何其他古代政治共同体都更广泛地吸纳外族人民，准许他们取得自己的公民权与名号，尽管确有一些罗马人谈论血统纯正。这种主张没有大量文献佐证，但它确实被提出过。
然而主导的逻辑是同化。一个通过社会共识形成、并且自知如此形成的共同体，仍然能够把自己塑造为一个血统共同体。正如关于古罗马的一段论述所言：

en: All Romans, no matter their origins, were in a sense descended from Romulus. . . . Commitment to the community allowed one to become part of that community. . . . Loyalty to the group was more important than biological ties in the construction of Roman society. . . . The myth of shared descent was by nature permeable.
zh: 所有罗马人无论出身如何，在某种意义上都是罗慕路斯的后裔。……只要忠于共同体，就能成为其中的一员。……在罗马社会的构成中，对群体的忠诚比血缘关系更重要。……共有祖先的神话本来就能容纳新的成员。

en: It remained permeable in Byzantium too, for the myth of shared descent and the assimilation of foreigners could coexist. It was common for premodern groups that formed through political integration to insist that they had a common origin, even in the face of the known facts: “Genealogical appeals are important for ethnic reasoning not because kinship and descent are ubiquitous or necessary aspects of how ethnicity or race were conceptualized in antiquity, but because they offer a central way of communicating a sense of ethnic / racial ‘fixity,’ essence, and continuity.”
zh: 在拜占庭，共有祖先的神话也能接纳新的成员，因为共享血统的神话与对外族的同化能够并存。通过政治整合形成的前现代群体，即便面对已知事实，也常常坚持自己拥有共同起源，这是司空见惯的：“在有关族群的论述中，援引谱系之所以重要，并非因为亲缘与血统是古代族群或种族概念化过程中无处不在或不可或缺的要素，而是因为援引谱系能够传达族群或种族‘固定不变’、具有某种本质并且延续至今的感觉，是表达这类看法的主要方式之一。”

en: A Fiction of the Sources?
zh: 史料的虚构？

en: The discussion has so far used explicit textual claims to outline the contours of the Roman community. People were included in it or excluded from it based on what are unambiguous ethnic criteria, as opposed to (say) criteria of occupation, gender, location, or socioeconomic status. We will flesh those ethnic criteria out in Chapter 3. One question remains to be asked here: Who made those “explicit textual claims”? We must ask this because it is theoretically possible, however unlikely, that this ethnic Roman community is a fiction of the source material. Historians should be suspicious of sources. In 1975, Cyril Mango referred to Byzantine literature as a “distorting mirror,” because its conventions of literary artifice distorted the historical reality that it ostensibly presented.

For example, many authors who wrote in a high register of Greek used concepts and even just a vocabulary that made their world appear more like classical antiquity than it really was. This insight was effectively a precursor to the Linguistic Turn, an understanding that dawned on many scholars in the 1980s and 1990s that our sources are literary artifacts that represent reality in ways that are conditioned by genre, various linguistic and cultural conventions, and political agendas. We do not have immaculate windows to Byzantine reality, but highly structured (and thereby “distorted”) images of it. Was Roman ethnicity one of its fictions?
zh: 迄今为止的讨论依据明确的文本表述来勾勒罗马共同体的轮廓。人们依据明白无误的族群标准被纳入或被排除于这个共同体之外，而非依据（比如说）职业、性别、地域或社会经济地位的标准。我们将在第3章充实这些族群标准。这里还有一个问题有待提出：是谁写下了那些“明确的文本表述”？我们必须追问这一点，因为虽不大可能，理论上仍不能排除，以族群为基础的罗马共同体是史料塑造出来的虚构。历史学家应当对史料保持怀疑。1975年，西里尔·曼戈把拜占庭文学称为一面“扭曲之镜”（distorting mirror），因为其文学表现手法的惯例，扭曲了它表面上呈现给人的历史现实。
例如，许多以高雅希腊语体写作的作者，使用的概念乃至仅仅是词汇，使他们的世界显得比实际更像古典古代。这一洞见实际上是“语言学转向”的先声——1980与1990年代许多学者逐渐领悟到：我们的史料是文学制品，它们以受体裁、各种语言与文化惯例以及政治议程制约的方式再现现实。我们并没有通往拜占庭现实的明净之窗，而只有高度结构化（因而“被扭曲”）的图像。罗马族群性是否就是其中的一种虚构？

en: In a recent iteration of the denialist thesis, Ioannis Stouraitis has asserted that it was. According to him, a tiny number of elite authors in Constantinople somehow conspired to manufacture a false picture, a rhetorical fiction, that the population of the empire constituted a homogenous Roman nation. However, he presents no actual evidence in support of his thesis, only assertions drawn from modern “critical theory.” He does not define this elite, which is a real problem for his thesis because the elite of the capital was drawn from the provinces. Nor does he explain why they would engage in such a distortion, or the mechanisms by which they perpetuated the fraud. Also, he couples this thesis with another one that directly contradicts it, namely that Romanness was claimed exclusively by the (tiny) ruling class in Constantinople, in contrast to the majority of the population, who were “ethno-culturally diverse.” He ignores the fact that the sources distinguish between Romans and ethnic minorities inside the empire, and even at the court. Moreover, the sources clearly do not limit Romanness to an elite, referring, for example, to “the leading men in the City [or state] and all who were of the Roman race.” In the end, the elite theory fails because it is not based on the sources and because it proposes a complex and incoherent solution to a nonexistent problem.
zh: 在否认论命题的一个晚近版本中，约安尼斯·斯图赖蒂斯断言罗马族群性确属虚构。据他说，君士坦丁堡极少数精英作者不知怎么合谋制造了一幅虚假图景、一种修辞虚构，即帝国人口构成了一个同质的罗马民族。然而他没有提出任何实际证据支持其命题，只有从现代“批判理论”中抽取的断言。他没有界定这个精英群体，而这使他的论点面临一个实质性问题，因为首都的精英来自各行省。他也没有解释他们为何要进行这种扭曲，或他们使这一骗局得以延续的机制。此外，他又提出一个与此直接矛盾的命题，即罗马性仅为君士坦丁堡（极少数）统治阶级所声称，与“族群文化上多元”的多数人口形成对照。他无视这样一个事实：史料区分了帝国内部的罗马人与族群少数群体，甚至在宫廷中亦然。而且，史料显然并未把罗马性局限于精英，例如它提到“都城［或国家］中的领袖人物以及所有属于罗马种族的人”。归根结底，精英理论之所以失败，是因为它不基于史料，并且为一个不存在的问题提出了复杂而不连贯的解答。

en: But the methodological question remains: Who produced the sources that tell us about Roman ethnicity? And did their representation distort it in ways for which we can perhaps correct? The answers to these questions are that, first, our sources were produced by such a wide variety of people across time, space, class, and language that no conspiracy to produce a “homogenizing discourse” can be suspected. We have evidence from outside Byzantium too, specifically from the Arab and even Latin worlds, that most Byzantines were ethnically Roman. And, second, there is reason to believe that the discursive practices of the Byzantine elite
the Romanness of the majority. They did not exaggerate it, far less invented it. Ethnic Romanness ran even
than our sources suggest. This discussion, then, is a good opportunity to expand the circle of the evidence and go closer to the ground.
zh: 但方法论问题依然存在：记述罗马族群性的史料是谁留下的？它们的再现是否以某种我们或许能够纠正的方式扭曲了它？这些问题的答案是：第一，我们的史料由跨越时间、空间、阶级与语言的极其多样的人群所生产，因此没有理由怀疑这些作者有意合谋制造一种“同质化话语”。我们也有来自拜占庭之外的证据，具体来自阿拉伯乃至拉丁世界，表明大多数拜占庭人在族群上是罗马人。第二，有理由相信拜占庭精英的话语实践
了多数人的罗马性。他们并未夸大它，更谈不上发明它。作为族群认同的罗马性，甚至比现存材料显示的扎根
。因此，这场讨论是一个扩大证据范围、让我们更贴近普通人的生活。

en: Provincial Syriac texts from the sixth century tell the same story. The Church of Zeugma, in Mesopotamia, wrote a letter to the Church of Edessa about an omen that concerned “you, us, and all Romans” (a goose had laid an egg with the inscription “the Romans will conquer”). This letter was then copied into the so-called chronicle of Pseudo-Joshua the Stylite, a Syriac text written by an official in Edessa that is as straightforwardly pro-Roman as any Greek or Latin history written in Constantinople.

It proves that members of a local church on the fringes of empire saw their fates as entwined with the victories of the Roman armies and considered themselves and their fellow provincials to be Romans.
zh: 六世纪的行省叙利亚语文本讲述了同样的故事。美索不达米亚的泽乌格马教会就一则关乎“你们、我们和所有罗马人”的预兆写信给埃德萨教会（一只鹅产下了一枚带有“罗马人将获胜”字样的蛋）。这封信随后被抄入所谓的《伪柱头修士约书亚编年史》，这是一部由埃德萨一名官员写成的叙利亚语文本，其亲罗马立场之直白，不亚于任何在君士坦丁堡写成的希腊语或拉丁语史书。
它证明，帝国边陲一个地方教会的成员把自己的命运与罗马军队的胜利紧密相连，并把自己和其他行省居民视为罗马人。

en: Examples can be multiplied, and more evidence pours in if we tap the riches of Arabic literature, which consistently called the Byzantines Romans
distinguishing them from other ethnic groups who lived near or among them, such as Slavs, Armenians, or Bulgarians.
Already in the eighth century, Arab writers listed the Romans among the “ethnic categories,” so alongside the Persians and Copts.
In their detailed testimony about Byzantium, Arab ethnographers and other writers treat the inhabitants of the empire, whether high or low, Constantinopolitan or provincial, as

unless they belonged to one of the aforementioned ethnic groups. The ninthcentury Arab essayist al-Jahiz quotes a Turkish general who made the point that Rum and Slav differ in the same way that Arab and non-Arab differ, not in the way that different kinds of Arabs differ.
Byzantine slave women in the Arab world were called “Rum women” and juxtaposed to other ethnicities, such as Slavs and Franks.
Texts mention slaves of Rum ethnic origin who had previously not been nobles but had practiced lowly professions, such as blacksmiths.
Al-Jahiz also claimed that the Rum of his time were good not at science but at the humble “handicrafts of turnery, carpentry, painting, and silk-weaving.”

He was not writing about an elite here—of generals, statesmen, and orators—but the general Rum population. Arab writers knew that there were civilian Rum in the towns and countryside of the empire as well as soldier Rum and elite Rum.

Arab ethnographers often relied on the testimony of visitors to the empire, none of whom reported that the Rum were limited to a small elite in the capital. They also traded with, captured, and interrogated the Rum, but if they found non-Roman ethnic identities among them that fell beneath the notice of our allegedly elite Byzantine sources, they failed to report it.
zh: 这样的例子可以成倍增加，而阿拉伯文献还能提供大量证据。这些文献一向将拜占庭人称作罗马人（
，鲁姆），将他们与生活在近旁或杂居的其他族群（如斯拉夫人、亚美尼亚人或保加尔人）区分开来。
早在八世纪，阿拉伯作者就把罗马人列入“族群类别”，与波斯人和科普特人并列。
在他们关于拜占庭的详尽见证中，阿拉伯民族志作者及其他作者把帝国居民——无论尊卑、无论君士坦丁堡人还是行省之人——都视为
（鲁姆人），除非他们属于上述族群之一。九世纪阿拉伯散文家贾希兹引用一位突厥将军的话指出：鲁姆人与斯拉夫人之间的差异，就如同阿拉伯人与非阿拉伯人之间的差异，而不是不同种类阿拉伯人之间的差异。
阿拉伯世界中的拜占庭女奴被称为“鲁姆女人”，与斯拉夫人、法兰克人等其他族群并列。
文本提到具有鲁姆族群出身的奴隶，他们先前并非贵族，而是从事铁匠等卑贱职业。
贾希兹还声称，他那个时代的鲁姆人擅长的不是科学，而是卑微的“旋削、木工、绘画和编织丝绸这些手艺”。
他这里写的不是精英——将军、政治家与演说家——而是普通的鲁姆人口。阿拉伯作者知道，帝国的鲁姆人有士兵和精英，也有居住在城镇和乡间的平民。
阿拉伯民族志作者往往依赖到访帝国者的见证，而这些人无一报告说鲁姆人仅限于首都一小撮精英。他们还与鲁姆人贸易、俘获并审讯他们，但即便他们在其中发现了那些被我们据称精英化的拜占庭史料所忽略的非罗马族群认同，他们也没有报告。

en: Moreover, Arab writers saw the Romans as a kinship group. The ninth-century Baghdadi poet Ibn al-Rumi claimed that he had Roman ancestors, and that his maternal uncles were Persian, but his paternal uncles were Romans.

A similar case is provided by the poet Abu Firas, a cousin of the Hamdanid prince of Aleppo Sayf alDawla. In the 960s, Abu Firas spent time as a captive in Constantinople. As it happens, his mother was Roman, a slave woman of his father, though Abu Firas defensively claimed she was a free woman. At any rate, he refers to her as Rum, which again proves that this was, in Arab eyes, an ethnic category, not one of class.

In this respect, therefore, the Arab and the Roman sources agree. However, the Arab writers cannot have been collaborating with the Byzantine elite to perpetuate a fiction of Roman ethnicity. They called them Romans because that was their self-professed ethnicity, whether in the army, the court, or the countryside.
zh: 此外，阿拉伯作者把罗马人视为一个亲缘群体。九世纪巴格达诗人伊本·鲁米声称自己有罗马祖先，他的舅父是波斯人，而他的叔伯是罗马人。
诗人阿布·菲拉斯提供了类似的例子，他是阿勒颇哈姆丹王朝埃米尔赛夫·道莱的堂兄弟。960年代，阿布·菲拉斯曾作为俘虏在君士坦丁堡度过一段时间。碰巧他的母亲是罗马人，是他父亲的一名女奴，尽管阿布·菲拉斯曾为她辩解，称她是自由女子。无论如何，他把她称为鲁姆人，这再次证明在阿拉伯人看来，这个称呼说的是她的族群归属，与她的社会阶层无关。
因此在这方面，阿拉伯史料与罗马史料是一致的。然而，阿拉伯作者不可能与拜占庭精英合谋延续罗马族群性的虚构。他们之所以称拜占庭人为罗马人，是因为那是拜占庭人自认的族群身份，无论在军队、宫廷还是乡村。

en: The same conclusion emerges even from some Frankish or Latin sources. Despite their general tendency to call the Byzantines “Greeks,” sometimes the real name sneaks through. This happened, for instance, when a western power wanted to keep the Byzantines loyal to an alliance and so softened the exclusion of the name Roman. In his diplomatic letters, the German emperor Friedrich II usually called his Byzantine counterpart Ioannes III Batatzes, his ally against the pope, “the emperor of the Greeks.” But in one letter of 1250 he indignantly recounts how the pope had excommunicated Batatzes and all his subjects—“all the Romans subject to you, shamelessly labelling as heretics the most orthodox Romans, from whom the Christian faith had spread originally to the four corners of the earth!” It was an occasional piece of flattery, to call his correspondent by his own ethnic name.
zh: 即便从某些法兰克或拉丁史料中也能得出同样的结论。尽管它们普遍倾向于把拜占庭人称为“希腊人”，真正的名号有时也会悄然浮现。例如，当一个西方强权想让拜占庭人忠于某项同盟、因而不再那么坚持排斥‘罗马人’这一称谓时，就会发生这种情况。德意志皇帝腓特烈二世在其外交书信中，通常把他那位对抗教皇的盟友、拜占庭君主约翰三世·瓦塔特泽斯称为“希腊人的皇帝”。但在1250年的一封信中，他愤慨地叙述教皇如何把瓦塔特泽斯及其所有臣民逐出教会——“所有臣属于您的罗马人，竟被无耻地打成异端，而基督信仰最初正是由这些信仰最为正统的罗马人传向大地四方！”这是一时兴起的奉承，用收信人自己的族群名号来称呼他。

en: This slip occurred in contexts that had nothing to do with Constantinople or the court. The

is an early fourteenth-century poem that recounts the conquest of the Peloponnese in the aftermath of the Fourth Crusade and the history of the Frankish principality of Achaea during the thirteenth century. In the Greek version of the poem, the Byzantines are called Romans throughout, including both the current subjects of the emperor and his former subjects now ruled by the French in the principality. These Romans are called a

throughout the poem and are defined by traits that were shared by all Byzantines, for example religion (e.g., v. 470: “to make all Romans obey the pope,” i.e., because they were Orthodox); ethnic stereotypes (e.g., vv. 593–594: the

of the Romans is crafty and faithless); and speech (“the language of the Romans”—what we call Greek—is here called ῥωμαίικα: v. 4130, i.e., “Roman-talk”; cf. v. 5207). Romans and Franks are juxtaposed as different but comparable types, and references are made to the “local Romans” of the Morea (e.g., v. 1424).
zh: 这种名号的流露发生在与君士坦丁堡或宫廷毫无关系的语境中。《摩里亚编年史》（
）是一部十四世纪初的诗作，叙述第四次十字军东征之后对伯罗奔尼撒的征服，以及十三世纪法兰克人亚该亚公国的历史。在这部诗作的希腊语版本中，拜占庭人自始至终被称为罗马人，既包括皇帝彼时的臣民，也包括如今在公国中受法兰克人统治的皇帝旧日臣民。这些罗马人在全诗中被称为一个族类（

），并由所有拜占庭人共享的特征来界定，例如宗教（如第470行：“使所有罗马人服从教皇”，即因为他们是正教徒）；族群刻板印象（如第593–594行：罗马人的族类狡诈而背信）；以及语言（“罗马人的语言”——我们所谓的希腊语——在此被称为ῥωμαίικα：第4130行，即“罗马话”；参第5207行）。罗马人与法兰克人作为彼此有别、却可以按同类标准看待的群体被并提，诗中还提到摩里亚的“本地罗马人”（如第1424行）。

This was, then, a Frankish text, reflecting the typical prejudice against the Romans (Byzantines), but it was composed in vernacular Greek by a Moreot Frank, who was possibly bilingual. In his poem he reflected local usage, including the fact that the Greek-speaking Orthodox population of the empire and its former provinces (such as the Peloponnese) called itself Roman and spoke

（希腊人）。这个问题尚未得到充分研究，但最近的一项研究认为，这首诗的希腊语版先于法语版，后者很可能译自希腊语版，并作了改编。
因此，这是一部法兰克文本，反映了针对罗马人（拜占庭人）的典型偏见，但它由一位摩里亚的法兰克人以通俗希腊语写成，此人可能通晓双语。这首诗反映出当时当地的用语，包括这样一个事实：帝国及其旧日行省（如伯罗奔尼撒）中讲希腊语的正教人口自称为罗马人，并讲
（罗马语）。

en: Additional proof is provided by the poem

written by the fourteenth-century Florentine poet Fazio degli Uberti. This didactic poem takes the form of an exploration of the known world. When the narrator reaches Macedonia he meets a local with whom he speaks in a demotic form of Greek, transcribed directly into the poem. “Do you speak Frangika?” (i.e., any Romance language), he asks the local. The latter answers “
(εἶμαι Ῥωμαῖος, i.e., I am a Roman).”

What he says immediately after that is harder to make out, but this testimony should lay to rest any doubt that the Byzantines called themselves Romans. Their enduring Roman ethnicity peaks through the cracks of western labels straight through to the Ottoman period. For example, the traveler Richard Chandler admitted in the eighteenth century that the Greeks of Athens called themselves and their language “Roman.”
French writers, such as Voltaire and Raffenel, made the same admission.
zh: 十四世纪佛罗伦萨诗人法齐奥·德利·乌贝尔蒂所写的诗作《迪塔蒙多》（
）提供了额外的证据。这部教诲诗采取探索已知世界的形式。当叙述者抵达马其顿时，他遇到一个当地人，并用一种通俗形式的希腊语与之交谈，这种希腊语被直接转写进诗中。“你会说
（法兰克话）吗？”（即任何一种罗曼语）他问当地人。后者回答“
（εἶμαι Ῥωμαῖος，即我是罗马人）”。
他接下来说的话较难辨明，但这一见证应当足以打消任何关于拜占庭人自称罗马人的疑虑。直到奥斯曼时期，罗马族群认同仍然延续，时而透过西方称谓的缝隙显露出来。例如，旅行家理查德·钱德勒在十八世纪承认，雅典的希腊人把自己及其语言称为“罗马的”。
伏尔泰、拉弗内尔等法国作者也作了同样的承认。

en: In sum, we are not dealing with a “distorting mirror” here or some elite “discourse” twisting reality for obscure reasons. There is no conceivable reason or mechanism that would enable Byzantine writers from the provinces and in many genres to conspire for over a thousand years to misinform their readers (and posterity) about the ethnicity of the majority population of their own society. This mechanism would, moreover, also have to explain how and why foreigners who were often the enemies of Romanía, such as the Arabs and occasionally the Franks too, supported this national discourse of homogenizing Romanness, if it corresponded to no existing Romans. And the testimony of other foreign observers can be added to theirs.

In addition, the conspiracy theory would have to explain why local “Greeks” in the Ottoman empire still referred to themselves and their language as “Roman,” as reported by western observers whose instinct and bias was to call them Greeks.
zh: 总之，我们这里面对的并不是一面“扭曲之镜”，也不是某种精英“话语”出于晦暗不明的原因扭曲现实。没有任何可以想见的理由或机制，能使来自行省、运用多种体裁的拜占庭作者合谋一千多年，就他们自己社会中多数人口的族群性误导其读者（乃至后世）。况且，这一机制还必须解释：如果这些强调罗马人同质性的民族论述并不对应任何真实存在的罗马人，那么那些往往与罗曼尼亚为敌的外族人——如阿拉伯人，偶尔还有法兰克人——如何以及为何会支持它。此外，还有其他外国观察者的见证可与之互证。
此外，合谋论还必须解释：为什么奥斯曼帝国中本地的“希腊人”仍然把自己及其语言称为“罗马的”，正如那些本能与偏见都倾向于称他们为希腊人的西方观察者所报告的那样。

en: Insofar as ethnicity is established primarily through discursive claims, which must be written in texts or inscriptions in order to reach us, we cannot hear the voice of the majority of the population. But Roman claims are made in all types of surviving sources, even those that bring us closest to the provincial ground level. They occur as far down the social scale as the sociology of Byzantine writing allows us to see, and there is no reason to believe that those claims then disappeared below the threshold of literacy. We have found no connection between being Roman and being able to read and write. Provincial saints’ lives, for example, assumed that the majority of the population (barring ethnic minorities) was Roman and that “we” were the targets of barbarian raids against “the Romans.” They sometimes expressed patriotic sentiments of loyalty and prayer for the emperor of the Romans.
zh: 既然族群性的确立主要依据文本中的说法，而这些说法必须见诸文字或铭刻才能传到我们手里，我们就无法听到多数居民自己的声音。不过，在各类存世材料里，都有人表明自己是罗马人，就连最贴近行省日常生活的材料也不例外。在拜占庭书写活动所能让我们看到的最低社会阶层中，这样的表述依然存在。没有理由相信，到了不识字的人中，这些说法就消失了。我们没有发现身为罗马人与识文断字之间有任何关联。比如，行省的圣徒传把多数居民（少数族群除外）是罗马人视为理所当然，认为蛮族袭击“罗马人”，袭击的就是“我们”。这些作品有时也表达爱国情感，表明忠于罗马人的皇帝，并为他祈祷。

en: In other words, these texts testify not only to Roman ethnicity but also to Roman patriotism. This was deeply embedded in provincial society. Beyond the hundreds of thousands of people who were sustained by and identified with the imperial state’s military infrastructure, religious services across the empire also typically ended in prayers on behalf of the emperor and for victory in war over the barbarians; the Church was a willing participant and supporter of imperial ideology.

Derek Krueger’s words of caution about religious differentiation in Byzantium are also relevant to the question of possible ethnic differentiation: “The religious lives of the elites and of the masses were not truly distinct. Rather, all Byzantines participated in a shared system of religious practice. . . . The religious lives and outlooks of the lower ranks of the clergy, in particular, may not have differed so greatly from those of their lay parishioners.”
zh: 换言之，这些文本不仅见证了罗马族群性，也见证了罗马爱国主义。它深深植根于行省社会。除了数十万依靠帝国军事基础设施供养、并与之认同的人之外，帝国各地的宗教仪式通常也以为皇帝祈福、祈求战胜蛮族的祷告作结；教会是帝国意识形态心甘情愿的参与者与支持者。
德里克·克鲁格关于拜占庭宗教分化的告诫之言，也适用于可能存在的族群分化问题：“精英与大众的宗教生活并非真正迥异。毋宁说，所有拜占庭人都参与了一套共享的宗教实践体系。……尤其是下层教士的宗教生活与观念，与其所在教区的平信徒相比，可能并没有那么大的差别。”

en: Besides, there was not a single elite in Byzantium. Generals, statesmen, and courtiers were invested in the Roman ideology of the imperial state because it underpinned their social status and power. But the literary elite based its status on the ability to write formal, purist Greek. It was this Hellenism that constituted their elite status, not their Romanness, which was “common” by comparison, in both senses. As Chapter 3 will show, in two crucial respects the literary elite’s stylistic preoccupations led it to

the Romanness of their world. Compelled to avoid vernacular terms and write as if they lived in ancient times, they had to pretend not to know what common people were calling the state in which they all lived and the language that they all spoke at home:
